# FIXME - review-findings log

The history of `dev` was squashed twice, as the owner ruled: after the review of the `focusInitial` fix, and before v0.0.14. This log names each commit by its subject as the reviewers read it, never by its hash, since a squash changes every hash. The branches `backup/dev-before-squash` and `backup/dev-before-squash-for-v0.0.14` keep the commits as the reviewers read them, and each commit of the first squash that merged several commits lists their subjects in its body.

Findings from reviews of llselect, newest round on top. Format spec (severity words, `[SEVERITY-N]` ids, Symptom/Cause/Fix/Verified labels, cross-round Q&A) lives in `../../CLAUDE.md` "Review-findings log". `N` is a stable id in creation order, not a rank; open items are `[ ]`, resolved `[x]`. No dates here - git log owns the when.

## review (the outside click default, round five)

Process: Codex Sol and Codex Astra, each in a fresh session at max effort, reviewed the fixes of the round below, "fix: [src][test][docs/llm] the touch hold ends at the press of a mouse or a pen", with the eight earlier answers on disk. Both found the library change holding: Codex Sol: "The library change holds on static inspection."; Codex Astra: "The library fixes hold on static inspection." Codex Sol: "High findings: none. Medium findings: none."; Codex Astra's one medium finding is in the questionnaire. Both found the two decisions of the agent sound: leaving the `pointerdown` of a touch to its `touchstart`, and one `zoomed-repeat` question for the zoomed page. Both found the test of the new end of the hold too narrow, which changes what a test checks, so a round six follows.

- [x] **[QUALITY-1030] - The test of the new end of the touch hold covered a mouse after the lift only**
  - Symptom: Codex Sol: "The regression covers only a mouse after `touchend`. The docs promise a mouse or pen press ends the entire hold. A regression that handles only `pointerType === 'mouse'`, or releases only after the touch ends, would pass." Codex Astra asked for the pen as well.
  - Fix: the test runs for a touch, a mouse and a pen, and a new test presses a mouse or a pen before the lift, after which a move of the finger is no longer blocked, the fix Codex Sol proposed.
  - Verified: a hold that ends at the press of a mouse only fails both tests for the pen; a hold that ends at such a press only after the lift fails the new test.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-1031] - A close when the fingers move, the drag questions, the length of the hold, and two records of the round below**
  - Symptom: the questionnaire mapped "the answer b or later" of `pinch-first-finger-alone` to the zoom value, while a close when the fingers move, the answer c, has no value, since the library asks the zoom setting once, when the second finger lands (Codex Astra). The open questions of Linux named two of the four drag questions that start with a press on an option (Codex Sol; Codex Astra), and no question asked for a drag from the closed select that ends outside the popup, a path that the record reports (Codex Sol). The docstring of `LLSelectScrollGestureBehavior` said that the hold lasts until a second finger lands, while the press of a mouse or a pen now ends it too (Codex Sol). The record of the round below gave both reviewers the whole list of missing questions (Codex Sol, as an unfaithful record), and said that Codex Astra found "a test that could not fail", where Codex Astra found two assertions whose failures could not fail their tests (Codex Astra, as an unfaithful record).
  - Fix: each corrected.

## review (the outside click default, round four)

Process: Codex Sol and Codex Astra, each in a fresh session at max effort, reviewed the fixes of the round below, "fix: [src][test][angularjs][docs/llm] the touch hold ignores clicks that no pointer made; a blocked press moves no focus", and the questionnaire as amended with that round's fixes, with the six earlier answers on disk. Both found the library fixes of the round below holding on static inspection, and its record faithful. Codex Sol found one more medium defect, in the older touch hold, and Codex Astra two assertions whose failures could not fail their tests. On the agent's decisions, both found sound the tap's swallow kept at its `mousedown`, Codex Astra: "A compatibility mousedown should preserve the non-mouse timeout and matching rules.", and the prevention of the `mousedown` inside the swallow; both agreed with mapping only the shared answers, and each found one more exception that the mapping must name. A finding needs a change to library code, and another to what a test checks, so a round five follows.

- [x] **[MEDIUM-1027] - The press of a mouse during the wait for a tap's click did not end the touch hold**
  - Symptom: Codex Sol: "A tap closes the popup and starts the one-second click wait. Before the tap's delayed click arrives, the user makes a mouse press near the touch-down. A mouse `pointerdown` does not end the touch hold. The hold therefore prevents the mouse `mousedown` and swallows the mouse click because the click has nonzero `detail`. The click belongs to a later pointer, not the tap." Older code.
  - Fix: the `pointerdown` of a mouse or a pen ends the touch hold, as a new press ends the swallow of a blocked outside press, the fix Codex Sol proposed. The `pointerdown` of a touch is left to its `touchstart`, which already ends the hold, so that the order in which a browser sends the two does not matter.
  - Verified: a new test in `test/behaviors.test.ts`: after the lift of a tap whose touch-down closed the popup, the `pointerdown` of a mouse lets the next `mousedown` and click through, while the `pointerdown` of a touch leaves both held. The test fails when the hold ignores the `pointerdown` of a mouse. The test of the hold's listeners now expects the `pointerdown` listener on the document, and its removal.
- [x] **[QUALITY-1028] - Two checks of the default of a click ran inside event listeners, where a failure could not fail the test**
  - Symptom: Codex Astra: "Both new `defaultPrevented === false` assertions run inside DOM event listeners. The local jsdom implementation catches listener exceptions. The default console configuration reports those exceptions without propagating them to the test."
  - Fix: the listener keeps the value, and the test body checks it, the fix Codex Astra proposed.
  - Verified: a swallow of a blocked outside press that prevents the default of a click whose `detail` is `0`, but lets the click through, fails the test of `test/outside-click.test.ts`; the same change to the touch hold fails the test of `test/behaviors.test.ts`.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-1029] - The pinch answers of a touchscreen, the close at the popup's edge, the coverage of the questionnaire, a sentence of `DESIGN.md`, two docstring leads, and a count**
  - Symptom: the questionnaire mapped a touchscreen pinch to `behaviorOfZoomGestureFn`, while the first finger can close the popup through `behaviorOfScrollGestureFn` before the zoom setting is asked (Codex Sol). It mapped a close when the finger leaves the popup to `'touch-drag'`, which a preset cannot copy, since a gesture carries no place of the finger (Codex Astra). The open questions left out the zoomed page in the other zones, the drags that start inside the popup, a close at the first move inside the popup, and the row height of Firefox on Windows (Codex Sol), and the touchpad pinch on Windows and the pinch on a zoomed page (Codex Astra). The first sentence of the swallow in `DESIGN.md` said that every press arms again at its `mousedown`, which the next sentence contradicted (Codex Sol). The leads of `TAP_CLICK_RADIUS` and `CLICK_WAIT_MS` were not sentences (Codex Sol). The record of the round below said "four trigger tests", where four calls sit in three tests (Codex Astra).
  - Fix: each corrected. A touchscreen pinch decides the zoom value only when the popup stayed open until the second finger, which `pinch-first-finger-alone` now asks for each place; `zoomed-repeat` replaces the two zoomed questions and covers every zone and the pinch; three drag questions and a fifth close moment are new.

## review (the outside click default, round three)

Process: Codex Sol and Codex Astra, each in a fresh session at max effort, reviewed the fixes of the round below, "fix: [src][test][angularjs][docs] the click swallow of a blocked outside press takes only the press's own click", and the new "docs: [docs/llm] the native select questionnaire", which the owner asked for during that round, with the four earlier answers on disk. Both found the fixes of the round below holding for the paths they named: Codex Sol: "The delayed tap wait, radius, and new-press cleanup hold on static inspection"; Codex Astra: "The delayed-click and unrelated-click fixes hold for the reported `base.ts` paths on static inspection". Each found one more medium defect, both in older code that the new default exposes: Codex Sol in the focus of a blocked press, and Codex Astra in the click swallow of the touch hold. Both found the record of the round below faithful. On the agent's decisions, Codex Sol found the use of `detail` "mostly sound", and Codex Astra agreed with it: "Testability alone would not justify the choice."; both found the separate bounds after a mouse press and after a tap reasonable, the arm again at `mousedown` reasonable, Codex Astra "for the measured compatibility sequence", and the new commit sound; on the questionnaire, Codex Sol found its structure "partly sound", and Codex Astra agreed with the owner's approach: "The common answers are useful, but their exceptions and coverage need correction." Two findings need a change to library code, so a round four follows.

- [x] **[MEDIUM-1022] - The click swallow of the touch hold took a click that no pointer made**
  - Symptom: Codex Astra: "Use the Chromium preset with outside-click blocking. Touch an outside control at `(10, 10)`. The touch-down closes the popup. If `onClose` calls another button's `click()`, that unrelated click is canceled." And: "the older touch hold checks coordinates only. The programmatic click's `(0, 0)` coordinates fall within the 32-pixel radius." Older code.
  - Fix: the touch hold ignores a click whose `detail` is `0` and goes on waiting, as the swallow of a blocked outside press does since the round below; its docs say so. Codex Astra's direction: "Ignore zero-detail clicks in the touch hold without ending its wait."
  - Verified: a new test in `test/behaviors.test.ts`: an `onClose` that calls `click()` on another button reaches that button with its default kept, and the click of the tap is still swallowed. The test fails when the touch hold takes a click whose `detail` is `0`. The simulated clicks of a tap in that file now have a `detail` of `1`, and four calls in three trigger tests use them in place of `click()`.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-1023] - A page handler that closed the popup at the pointerdown let the mousedown move focus**
  - Symptom: Codex Sol: "An outside button has a `pointerdown` handler that calls `sel.close()` without moving focus. Closing removes `blockMouseDownHandler`. The following `mousedown` is therefore not default-prevented. The browser focuses the button and fires `onBlur`, although the page handler moved no focus. The surviving click swallow still blocks the click." Older code, which the focus docs expose.
  - Fix: while armed, the swallow also prevents the default of an outside `mousedown`, so the browser moves no focus after such a close either, the fix Codex Sol proposed: "Keep a transient `mousedown` default-preventer for the armed press after the popup closes."
  - Verified: a new test in `test/outside-click.test.ts`: after a page handler closes the popup at the `pointerdown`, the `mousedown` is default-prevented, the click is swallowed, focus stays on the trigger, and `onBlur` does not run. The test fails without the new listener.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-1024] - The mousedown of a tap could shorten the tap's swallow**
  - Symptom: the `mousedown` listener of `'block'` armed the swallow again as a mouse press, which ends in the task after its release. Codex Astra noted that a browser may send the compatibility events of a tap among its pointer events: "Compatibility events may instead be interleaved with pointer events." If the `mousedown` of a tap came before the tap's `pointerup`, while the popup was open, and the popup then closed, the release task ended the swallow before a click that the browser held back, found by the agent from that note.
  - Fix: the `mousedown` arms again as a mouse press only when no press that is not a mouse press armed the swallow; the comment no longer assumes an order of the tap's events.
  - Verified: a new test in `test/outside-click.test.ts`: the `mousedown` of a tap before its lift, a page handler that closes the popup there, and the click 300 ms after the lift: the click is swallowed. The test fails when the `mousedown` arms again as a mouse press.
- [x] **[QUALITY-1025] - The tests of the swallow did not check that the default action of the click was prevented**
  - Symptom: Codex Astra: "Removing only the guard's `preventDefault()` would leave those assertions satisfied. An outside link could then navigate despite the promised blocking."
  - Fix: the click helper of `test/outside-click.test.ts` returns its event, and each test of the swallow checks that a swallowed click is default-prevented and that a click that gets through is not.
  - Verified: a swallow without `preventDefault()` fails five tests.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-1026] - The questionnaire's mapping and coverage, the arm described against the code, finding ids as names, and the leads of two docstrings**
  - Symptom: the last section of the questionnaire mapped "the click and tap questions" and "the zoom questions" to values, while `click-on-select` and `pinch-first-finger-alone` have answers of their own, and its lead said that every answer sets a preset value (Codex Sol; Codex Astra). The open questions left out the Ctrl wheel inside the popup, the mouse drags on Windows and in Safari, the touchpad scroll on Linux, WebKit's pinches and drags, a page that is already zoomed, a swipe that lifts outside the popup and Edge, listed `click-on-select` twice for Windows, and called the rest answered (Codex Sol; Codex Astra). "Any page with a native `<select>` serves" let a customizable select in, and a page at its scroll limit cannot show a scroll (Codex Astra). `DESIGN.md` said that the `mousedown` arms only where no `pointerdown` armed, while the code arms again at every outside `mousedown` (Codex Sol; Codex Astra). The record of the round below named findings by their ids (Codex Sol; Codex Astra). The docstrings of `TAP_CLICK_RADIUS` and `CLICK_WAIT_MS` had more than one lead sentence (Codex Astra).
  - Fix: each corrected. The questionnaire maps only the questions with the shared answers, says what each question with its own answers is evidence for, gains the missing questions and platform rows, and names the ordinary native select of demo 17.1 and the checks before a scroll or a zoom question.

## review (the outside click default, round two)

Process: Codex Sol and Codex Astra, each in a fresh session at max effort, reviewed the first commit after the fixes of the round below, and the rename that the owner ruled during that round, "refactor: [src][angularjs][demo][test][docs][scripts] behaviorOf names for the three behavior settings", with the two answers of the round below on disk. Both found that the click swallow for a press during which a page handler moves focus (MEDIUM-1015) lets through a tap's click that a browser holds back, and both rated it medium; Codex Astra found a second medium defect of the same swallow. Codex Sol found the other fixes holding: "MEDIUM-1014 holds.", "QUALITY-1016 holds.", "QUALITY-1017 holds."; Codex Astra found the Firefox correction and the evidence qualifications holding "on static inspection", and the enum fallback, the default test and the AngularJS test right. On the rename, Codex Sol: "The rename scope is sound and complete."; Codex Astra: "Renaming the dependent API names is sound. Historical passages inside otherwise live documents also need preservation." Both found no old name left in a live file and the key of the marks shared by the bundles. On the agent's decisions, both found the arm at `pointerdown` justified, Codex Sol: "necessary and correctly covers a focus change before `mousedown`", and the end in the task after the release too short for a tap; both found `null` with a check at each caller sound, Codex Astra: "Returning `undefined` without changing callers would lose provider defaults."; both found the README's reason first sound, and Codex Astra asked for one lead sentence. Two findings need a change to library code, so a round three follows.

- [x] **[MEDIUM-1019] - The swallow of a blocked tap ended before the click that a browser holds back**
  - Symptom: Codex Sol: "On a touch page without a mobile viewport, an outside button's `pointerdown` handler focuses the button. The resulting `focusout` closes the popup. `pointerup` then schedules disarming with `setTimeout(..., 0)`, but a compatibility click may arrive roughly 300 ms later, as the existing `CLICK_WAIT_MS` comment in `src/behaviors.ts` already recognizes. The delayed click therefore activates the outside button under `'block'`." Codex Astra described the same case. The tests dispatched the release and the click in one task (both).
  - Fix: after a press that is not a mouse press, the swallow waits `CLICK_WAIT_MS` after the `pointerup`, the wait of the touch hold, and takes only a click within `TAP_CLICK_RADIUS` of the touch-down, the radius of the touch hold; `src/behaviors.ts` now exports both. The `pointerdown` of a new press ends the swallow, as the next touch ends the touch hold. Codex Sol's direction: "For a touch-origin press, retain the swallow until a matching click or a bounded delayed-click timeout, using the existing one-second tap window and coordinate correlation as the model."
  - Verified: two new tests in `test/outside-click.test.ts`, with mocked timers: the click of a tap 300 ms after the lift is swallowed, and a click far from the touch-down is not; the swallow ends a second after the lift, and at the `pointerdown` of a new tap close to the first. Each of four mutations failed one of them: no wait after a tap; no radius; no end at a new press; the pointer type read as a mouse.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-1020] - A click that the press did not make ended the swallow**
  - Symptom: Codex Astra: "An outside button focuses itself during `mousedown`. The resulting `onBlur` callback calls another button's `click()`. The new guard cancels that unrelated click and unconditionally disarms. The original physical click then reaches the outside button." And: "The guard receives no information identifying the press. Any click can consume it, including a keyboard click while the mouse remains held."
  - Fix: only a click whose `detail` is not `0` counts as the click of the press, since the keyboard and `click()` give `0`; any other click passes and leaves the swallow armed. Codex Astra's direction: "Match the click to the armed press. Ignore unrelated clicks without disarming."
  - Verified: a new test: an `onBlur` that calls `click()` on another button reaches that button, and the click of the press is still swallowed; the test fails when the swallow takes a click whose `detail` is `0`. The earlier tests now dispatch the click of a pointer, whose `detail` is `1`.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-1021] - An article that the rename left, the promise of no blur, two completed items renamed, a dropped condition, and the README lead**
  - Symptom: "A preset also holds an `behaviorOfOutsideClick`" in `angularjs/API.md`, and "Each preset also holds an `behaviorOfOutsideClick`" in `DESIGN.md` (Codex Sol). The `onBlur` docstring, the `ll-on-blur` entry and two bullets of `DESIGN.md` promised that an outside press under `'block'` fires no blur, while a page handler that moves focus during the press fires it, older words that the case of a page handler moving focus during the press (MEDIUM-1015) shows false (Codex Astra). The rename changed the names in two completed items of `TODO.md`: the record of the zoom presets, where both consultants had recommended `zoomGestureToBehaviorFn`, and the item P1-b (Codex Astra, as an unfaithful record). The symptom of the AngularJS enum finding (QUALITY-1016) left out the gesture function of Codex Astra's finding (Codex Astra, as an unfaithful record). The README section opened with three sentences (Codex Astra: "`CLAUDE.md` requires one lead sentence and further facts in bullets.").
  - Fix: each corrected; the two completed items keep the names of their time and end with a note on the rename. The docstring of `armOutsidePressClickSwallow` and the bullet of `DESIGN.md` on that swallow (MEDIUM-1015) now say when the click of a tap comes, in place of "the same task as its release" for every press.

## review (the outside click default)

Process: Codex Sol and Codex Astra, each in a fresh session at max effort, reviewed "feat: [src][angularjs][demo][test][docs][scripts] outsideClickBehavior defaults to 'block' and joins the behavior presets". Both found the wrong value of the Firefox-on-Windows preset, and both rated it medium; Codex Sol found one more medium defect, in older code that the new default exposes to every select component without the setting. Neither found anything in the core's reading of the default and of a preset's value, the type-only import and the exports, the touch hold for a valid value, the open shadow roots, the trigger buttons strip, or the `<ui-llselect>` line and its comment. On the agent's decisions, both agreed with reading the default from the default preset, with the required preset field, with the AngularJS attribute without a provider key, with the fixed `'pass-through'` of `<ui-llselect>`, with the order of demo section 3 and with the place of the README section. On the values of the platform presets, Codex Astra: "Agree with the structure. Firefox's value needs correction; Safari's evidence needs qualification. Chromium's supplied source supports pass-through."; Codex Sol: "Sound in structure, but not in evidence or values. Firefox Windows must be pass-through. Safari remains provisional." On stating the native behavior of Chrome and Edge on Windows from the source alone, Codex Astra: "The inference is supported. Describe the result as source-based until the Windows hand test confirms it."; Codex Sol: "Not sound as written. The source establishes upstream Chromium behavior, not an independently verified Edge result." Codex Astra found the records of the owner's words faithful, and Codex Sol found them faithful but for the comment ruling (DOCUMENTATION-1018). The agent read the Firefox finding in `SelectParent.sys.mjs` and `nsXULPopupManager.cpp` and confirmed it. While the round ran, the owner ruled new names for the three behavior settings; the rename follows in a commit of its own, after these fixes. Later, the owner ruled the other order of demo section 3, in the owner's words, translated from Chinese: "the order of examples 3.1 and 3.2 has to be swapped"; the default, `'block'`, is now 3.1, and `'pass-through'` is 3.2.

- [x] **[MEDIUM-1014] - The Firefox-on-Windows preset blocked the outside click, while Firefox on Windows lets it through**
  - Symptom: Codex Astra: "`SelectParent._createMenulist()` sets `consumeoutsideclicks="false"` on Windows. `ConsumeOutsideClicks()` therefore returns `ConsumeOutsideClicks_ParentOnly` before reaching the cited `menulist` fallback. That policy consumes clicks over the anchor, allowing clicks elsewhere through." Codex Sol: "An app spreads `behaviorPresetsOfFirefoxOnWindows`, opens the popup, and clicks an outside button. llselect swallows the click, while Firefox on Windows lets the outside control receive it." The preset's docstring, the README, the hints of demo section 3, `DESIGN.md` and `TODO.md` said that Firefox blocks the click on every operating system.
  - Cause: the agent's reading of the source stopped at the `menulist` case of `nsMenuPopupFrame::ConsumeOutsideClicks` and its comment, and missed the attribute that the function reads first.
  - Fix: the preset holds `'pass-through'`, the fix both proposed; its docstring, the README, the hints, `DESIGN.md` "Outside click while the popup is open" and `TODO.md` follow, and the README and the hints now say what the native select does on each operating system.
  - Verified: the preset test in `test/outside-click.test.ts` expects `'pass-through'`, and fails with `'block'`. The agent read the attribute in `SelectParent._createMenulist()`, its use in `nsMenuPopupFrame::ConsumeOutsideClicks`, and the consume step of `nsXULPopupManager::RollupInternal`.
  - Q: Why does the native select of Firefox let the click through on Windows, while `ConsumeOutsideClicks` comments "Consume outside clicks for combo boxes on all platforms"?
    - A: Because that comment belongs to the case of a popup without the attribute `consumeoutsideclicks`, and on Windows `SelectParent._createMenulist()` sets the attribute to `false`, which `ConsumeOutsideClicks` reads first: `ConsumeOutsideClicks_ParentOnly` consumes only a click over the select itself.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-1015] - A page handler that moved focus during a blocked outside press let the click through**
  - Symptom: Codex Sol: "An outside button's `mousedown` handler calls `button.focus()`. The document capture listener prevents the default, but propagation continues. The scripted focus move fires `focusout`, which closes the select component and removes the click capture listener. The following click reaches the button, despite `'block'`." The code is older, and the new default exposes it to every select component without the setting; the regression test of the race never moved focus once the press was default-prevented (Codex Sol). A `pointerdown` handler that moves focus did the same, found by the agent. Measured by the agent with Playwright's mouse in Chromium 156, Firefox 153 and WebKit 26.5: the click reached a button whose `mousedown` or `pointerdown` handler focused it.
  - Fix: each outside press under `'block'` arms a one-shot swallow of its click at its `pointerdown` and at its `mousedown`, and the close leaves the swallow armed; the click ends it, and so do the task after the release, a `pointercancel` and `destroy()`. Codex Sol's direction: "Keep a one-shot click swallow armed after a blocked outside mousedown, even if `focusout` closes the popup." The arm at `pointerdown` is the agent's.
  - Verified: two new tests in `test/outside-click.test.ts`: when a page handler moves focus at the `pointerdown` or at the `mousedown`, the popup closes during the press and its click is still swallowed; after a release without a click, a `pointercancel` or `destroy()`, a later click reaches the button. Each of six mutations failed one of them: no arm; no arm at `pointerdown`; a disarm at the release itself; no disarm after the release; none at `pointercancel`; none in `destroy()`. In the same three engines, the click no longer reached either button, the popup closed, and a later Enter on the focused button still clicked it.
- [x] **[QUALITY-1016] - An AngularJS enum attribute that was not a string kept its value, while its warning said that the default applies**
  - Symptom: Codex Astra: "For `ll-outside-click-behavior="false"`, the helper warns "Falling back to the default" but returns `false`." With that value and a gesture function that closes the popup at an outside touch-down and lets the page scroll, the mouse path of the core read the value as `'block'`, while the touch hold, which reads `'block'` only, let the click of the tap through (Codex Astra: "Combine that attribute with a gesture function that closes on outside touch-down and allows scrolling."). The helper `evalEnumAttr` serves five attributes; for `ll-popup-width-policy` and `ll-color-scheme`, the invalid value also replaced the app-wide default of `llselectConfigProvider`, found by the agent.
  - Fix: `evalEnumAttr` returns `null` for a value that is not a string, as `evalNumberAttr` does, and its five callers then keep the default, the app-wide one included. Codex Astra's direction was to return `undefined`; with the callers unchanged, that would have dropped the app-wide default too.
  - Verified: a new test in `angularjs/test/llselect-angularjs.test.mjs`: `ll-outside-click-behavior="false"` and `ll-popup-width-policy="fit-content"` warn, and the select component keeps `'block'` and the app-wide `'match-trigger-wrapper'`. The test fails when the helper returns the invalid value again.
- [x] **[QUALITY-1017] - The new tests did not check the focus claim, nor `<llselect-multiple>`**
  - Symptom: the default test of `test/outside-click.test.ts` named focus, but never focused the select component nor checked the active element (Codex Astra; Codex Sol, who asked to check `onBlur` too). The AngularJS test of the outside click covered `<llselect-single>` only, while its name speaks of both directives (Codex Astra).
  - Fix: the default test focuses the trigger, makes the focus move that a browser makes for a press that is not default-prevented, and checks the active element and that `onBlur` did not run; the AngularJS test runs for both directives.
  - Verified: the default test fails when the outside `mousedown` is not default-prevented.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-1018] - Browser claims beyond the evidence, the old default, a missing break, a generalized ruling, and the reason after the explanation**
  - Symptom: the module docstring of `src/behavior-presets.ts` said that every platform value follows the browsers' source code, and the conclusion of the new `DESIGN.md` section took the macOS result as established, while the Safari value is an inference (Codex Astra; Codex Sol). `DESIGN.md` said that Chromium shows the menu of the operating system on macOS and Android, while the cited flag establishes only an external popup menu, and the README and the hints stated Chrome and Edge as facts from the source of upstream Chromium (Codex Sol). The bullet "Where the listeners sit" of `DESIGN.md` "Scroll gestures while the popup is open" still said "under the default `outsideClickBehavior: 'pass-through'`", older text that the new default made false (Codex Astra; Codex Sol). The breaking-change bullet left out that an app's own object typed as `LLSelectBehaviorPreset` must now name `outsideClickBehavior` (Codex Astra; Codex Sol), and the row of `LLSelectBehaviorPreset` in `naming-conventions.md` listed `scrollGestureToBehaviorFn` alone, older text that already left out `zoomGestureToBehaviorFn` (Codex Sol). The docstring of `LLSelectOutsideClickBehavior` said "Focus stays in the select component.", and the matching bullet of `A11Y.md` said the same, while focus that was elsewhere stays elsewhere (Codex Sol). `angularjs/DESIGN.md` "Behavior follows ui-select" turned the owner's request for the comment on the bridge's `outsideClickBehavior` line into a rule for every such line (Codex Sol, as an unfaithful record). The README section and the hint of demo section 3 gave the reason for the default after the explanation, and one README bullet held two facts (Codex Astra).

## review (the up-down arrows, round two)

Records: the Process line of the round below said that neither reviewer had found a path that leaves a positioner or a listener behind, while both had reported such paths where an error is thrown (Codex Astra); and the entry on the doc rules named `PositionInput` alone and said "each corrected", while Codex Astra had named `PositionerOptions` as well, whose docstrings were not corrected (Codex Sol).

The four `angularjs/API.md` entries and the two fields of `PositionerOptions` have one lead sentence and bullets. The README row stays a one-line summary of a table: with negative values gone, what it leaves out is a trigger wrapper outside the viewport and a margin wider than half of it, which the reference of the two settings states.

## review (the basic guard and the popup distance settings)

Process: Codex Sol and Codex Astra, each in a fresh session at max effort, reviewed the four newest commits: the stopped open as the owner's ruling cut it back, the review rounds closed under that ruling, and "feat: [src][angularjs][test][docs] popupDistanceFromTriggerWrapper and popupDistanceFromViewportEdge settings". The brief named what the ruling makes unsupported use, and gave both reviewers the six earlier answers on disk. Codex Sol: "All six external reviewer records were readable and checked." Neither found a path on which a function that closes, destroys or reopens the select component during `open()`, and returns without throwing, leaves a positioner or a listener behind, and neither found a leftover of the three removed guards. Both found what a `close()` that throws leaves behind, Codex Astra also what a notification leaves behind that throws at the positioner's first placement, and each found one error in the math of the new settings. Every fix below changed library code or what a test checks, except the last entry.

- [x] **[MEDIUM-987] - `destroy()` stopped at a `close()` that threw, and left an open popup attached**
  - Symptom: Codex Sol: "If an overridden `close()` throws before `super.close()`, `destroy()` exits before its fallback. An open popup can retain its positioner, `ResizeObserver`, and document, window, visual-viewport, root or popup listeners. If the override throws after `super.close()`, the remaining label, color-scheme and root-element cleanup is still skipped." Codex Astra: "A `close()` override that throws before `super.close()` bypasses the new fallback and the remaining teardown." An `onClose` listener that throws skipped the same steps, which the agent added to the case. The behavior is older than the guard; the fallback of the guard did not cover it.
  - Fix: the teardown of `destroy()` runs in a `finally`, both reviewers' direction, and the error of the close goes on to the caller. No step of that teardown calls a function of the settings or an overridable method any more, so no second error can take the place of the first (MEDIUM-989). A close that throws after it marked the popup closed still got past this fix (MEDIUM-994).
  - Verified: two tests in `test/open-superseded.test.ts`: a `close()` override that throws before it closes, after an open that attached the positioner and the listeners, and an `onClose` listener that throws. In both, `destroy()` throws the error, no listener stays on the document or on the window, and the root element is empty. Both fail without the `finally`.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-988] - A notification that threw at the positioner's first placement left the positioner's listeners behind**
  - Symptom: Codex Astra: "The first placement can close through `onHide`, then encounter a throwing `onClose` notification. The positioner has already registered listeners and its `ResizeObserver`, but never returns its handle. Neither `close()` nor the abandoned-open check can detach it. A later `destroy()` finds `opened === false` and cannot recover those resources." Each later scroll or resize then re-placed a closed popup. The behavior is older than the guard.
  - Fix: `createPositioner` runs the first placement before it registers anything. Codex Astra's own direction was another one: "dispose registrations when initial placement throws, then rethrow. Preserve the newer positioner's placement if reopening occurred."
  - Verified: a test in `test/positioning.test.ts`: with an `onHide` that throws at the first placement, no listener is added on the window or on the visual viewport, no `ResizeObserver` is built, and the popup has no inline style. It fails with the first placement after the registrations.
  - Q: Why move the first placement, not catch its error and detach?
    - A: Because a detach clears the inline styles of the popup, which a newer positioner shares when the listener reopened before it threw; the caller would then have to place the popup again from inside a `catch`. With nothing registered yet, there is nothing to detach and nothing to repair.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-989] - A close from `onOpen` or `onOpened` called the arrow's content function twice**
  - Symptom: Codex Sol: "An `onOpen` listener is allowed to call `close()`. That close renders the closed arrow once. The superseded check then calls `abandon()`, which runs `clearOpenState()` again and invokes `createTriggerArrowContentElFn` a second time. Before this commit, the supported `onOpen` path rendered the closed arrow only once." A close from `onOpened` did the same. Codex Astra named the same call from the other side: the cleanup that `destroy()` falls back on "still calls the arrow content function".
  - Fix: `clearOpenState` no longer renders the arrow, and calls no content function, no predicate and no overridable method. `close()` renders the arrow right after it, as before, and a call of `open()` that stopped at its own arrow render renders the arrow once more, since that render had committed the arrow of the open state after the close. Codex Sol's own direction was another one: "Let checks after `onOpened` and `onOpen` restore scroll and stop without repeating `clearOpenState()` when the select component stayed closed."
  - Verified: two tests in `test/open-superseded.test.ts`, for a close from `onOpen` and from an `onOpened` override: the arrow's content function runs once for the open state and once for the closed state. Both fail when the arrow render is back in `clearOpenState`. The test of an arrow content function that closes fails without the second render.
  - Q: Why take the arrow out of the cleanup, not skip the cleanup after a notification?
    - A: Because the same change answers both findings. A cleanup that calls no function of the settings can run a second time after any step without calling the arrow's content function again, though it repeats its DOM writes, and `destroy()` can fall back on it without calling into an app whose `close()` just failed.

  - Symptom: Codex Astra: "Consider a visible vertical interval `[100, 500]`, an anchor spanning `[50, 80]`, and a tall popup. Set the anchor distance to `-20` and the viewport distance to `8`. The calculation produces `belowStart = 80` and `maxHeight = 412`. It then clamps `top` to `100` without adjusting the height. The popup can end at `512`, beyond the viewport, instead of the requested `492`."

This round counted a negative distance as 0 at a stand-in edge only, against Codex Astra's own direction, "restrict the final clamp to the no-room case, preserving the signed-distance calculation when room exists". The arrow test kept a list of states that nothing read (Codex Astra).

No test said what a stopped call does with the window scroll; two tests now do, for a closed and for a destroyed select component.

The README bullet on that rule gave the rule before its reason (Codex Astra). The two settings docstrings and DESIGN.md "Popup distances" called the viewport the visual viewport, while a browser without that API, such as desktop Firefox below 91, gives the layout viewport (Codex Sol); they promised a width of at most the viewport's width minus twice the distance, which is negative for a large distance, and margins that do not hold once no room is left (Codex Astra). Process: Codex Sol and Codex Astra, each in a fresh session at max effort, reviewed the two commits again after the fixes of round one. The agent stopped the loop here: two rounds each brought out more steps that write after app code, so guarding the steps one by one has no end in sight. The agent then asked both reviewers, each in a fresh session, which approach to take, and the owner ruled for the basic guard: `open()` keeps its guard, the three guards of round one are gone, and a function that builds or decides must not change the select component. `DESIGN.md` "Functions that build or decide" holds the rule, both reviewers' recommendations in their own words, and the ruling. A function of one of those rows that called `setChosenItem()` or `toggleItem()` updated the rows of the previous render, or none at the first open, and the render then committed its rows from before the call: the item was chosen, and its row said `aria-selected="false"` (Codex Sol, with a multiple select component and `toggleItem()`; Codex Astra, with a single select component and an action row's `textFn` that calls `setChosenItem('b')`).

    - A: Because the guard kept the rows local until the commit, and an in-place row update reads the row field while the rows are built. Moving a write changes the order for everything that reads what it wrote.

  - Symptom: `recomputeFilteredItems` stored an outdated gather's result in `filteredItems`, though the gather no longer cached it, so that new rows stood beside old visible items (Codex Sol, for a `setItems()` during the gather with the popup left open; Codex Astra, for a close, new items and a reopen). The owner's ruling makes that unsupported use, so the library adds no guard for it, and what the popup shows afterwards is not defined (`DESIGN.md` "Functions that build or decide"). The writes named above still happen, and the gather's guard went with the two others, so an outdated gather is cached again.

In this log, the entry on the stopped open names its cases, and its answer on the second run of the closed state holds again, now that the list render and the arrow render commit as before; the entry on the overtaken writes no longer has a fix to describe; the Process line of round one names the finding in words.

  - Symptom: `compileTemplateSlot` (`angularjs/llselect-ui-select.js:240`) compiles a row's or the trigger's template and, outside a digest, runs a digest of the new child scope, inside the content function that the core calls while it builds the list or the trigger. The bridge's `renderPopupList` override also destroys the scopes of the old rows before the core builds the new ones (`releaseRowScopes`, `angularjs/llselect-ui-select.js:261`). Both reviewers named it in the consultation. Codex Sol, on the bridge: "runs a child-scope digest synchronously while building row and trigger templates. It also destroys old row scopes from rendering overrides. Both operations can run app code." Codex Astra: "The installed AngularJS source confirms that pending `$evalAsync` work can make that child digest traverse the root. ## review (the report from an app that uses 0.0.12)

Process: the owner uses `@llselect/core` in an app of the owner's own, and the agent that works on that app wrote a report on version 0.0.12, with a page that reproduces its first point. The report is kept outside the repository. The owner passed on that agent's summary: one bug, which the summary calls serious, and two smaller points. The summary on the bug, translated from Chinese: the silent failure "is more trouble than the bug itself".

- [x] **[HIGH-972] - In a SimpleBar scroll area, no popup opened, and nothing said why (0.0.12)**
  - Symptom: the report: `open()` returned at the hidden-trigger check for a trigger that was fully visible. The trigger sat in absolutely positioned content whose containing block lies outside an `overflow: hidden` ancestor, and that ancestor had a width of 0. SimpleBar builds this: its wrapper has `overflow: hidden` and takes its size from an in-flow placeholder, while the content sits in an absolutely positioned mask whose containing block is the SimpleBar root. In the reporting app the wrapper "measured 1039px wide at rest and 0px from the first click on". Nothing was logged.
  - Cause: version 0.0.12 tested the trigger against every ancestor that clips, whether or not that ancestor's clip applies to the trigger, the cause that an earlier report on a page scroll lock had already brought out (HIGH-796).
  - Fix: none needed. The hidden-trigger check walks the containing-block chain (HIGH-796), and a refused `open()` warns in the console (QUALITY-798), since the commits before the tag `v0.0.13`. Version 0.0.12 is the newest on npm, so the fix reaches that app with the next release.

Version 0.0.12 refuses the report's case B and the zero-width state, with an empty console.   - Symptom: the other agent's summary, which the owner passed on: the 4 px between the popup and the trigger box are hard-coded and cannot be set. The report file does not name this point. The distance was the constant `GAP` of `src/positioning.ts`. CSS cannot change it correctly either, since the positioner computes the popup's place and its `maxHeight` from it.

Two tolerances of one pixel are fixed as well: the end of a scroll in `canScroll` (`src/behaviors.ts`) and the allowance in `measureNaturalWidth` (`src/positioning.ts`).

AngularJS has the attributes `ll-popup-distance-from-trigger-wrapper` and `ll-popup-distance-from-viewport-edge`, and app-wide defaults of the settings' names, which `<ui-llselect>` takes too. The other fixed numbers stay fixed, by the agent's own view; the owner did not rule on them. Owner rulings, each translated from Chinese. First: "A new setting, but I want to know where you put it; the meaning of the noun is too odd." Then, on the agent's three names and its question whether the 8 px should become a setting too: "Distance; and are these two to go into an interface of their own, or straight into the root settings?" The agent read "these two" as both distances, and said so. Last, on the agent's recommendation of the root: "Put them at the root." `DESIGN.md` "Popup distances" holds the contract and the reasons.

Measured headless in Chromium 156, Firefox 153 and WebKit 26.5: the distance to the trigger wrapper for 4, 12 and 0, below it; the room to the bottom edge for 8, 20 and 0 with a list too tall to fit; a popup above the trigger wrapper that starts at the top room; the side margin and the width limit under `'fit-content'`, in both directions; and no side margin under `'match-trigger-wrapper'`. Not measured on a pinch-zoomed page or on a phone.
- [ ] **[QUALITY-986] - Above the trigger wrapper, the popup sits up to half a pixel off its distance**
  - Symptom: found while the two distance settings were measured (QUALITY-974). With a three-row popup above the trigger wrapper, the distance for a setting of 4 measured 3.828 px in Chromium 156 and WebKit 26.5 and 3.750 px in Firefox 153; for 12, 11.828 px and 11.750 px; for 0, -0.172 px and -0.250 px, so the popup overlapped the trigger wrapper slightly. Below the trigger wrapper the distance was exact in every case, and so was a popup above it whose height the positioner limits.
  - Cause: for a popup above the trigger wrapper, `computePosition` subtracts the popup's height from the place of its bottom edge. `reposition` in `createPositioner` reads that height from `offsetHeight` (`src/positioning.ts:754`), a whole number, while the popup was 87.172 px high in Chromium and WebKit and 87.250 px in Firefox. The error is older than the two settings: the fixed 4 px had it too.
  - Impact: at most half a pixel in the measured cases, above the trigger wrapper only. Not measured, derived from the code: when the popup's natural height is less than about 1.5 px over its height limit, the three whole-pixel reads of `reposition` can come out under the limit, and the popup then overlaps its distance by up to that much. It matters most at a distance of 0, where the two edges are meant to meet. The docstring of `popupDistanceFromTriggerWrapper` states both limits.
  - Fix: open; `TODO.md` "Positioning precision" has tracked the whole-pixel reads since the width fix. One direction: read the fractional height from the computed style, guarded by `offsetHeight`, as `measureNaturalWidth` does for the width.

Process: Codex Sol and Codex Astra, each in a fresh session at max effort, reviewed "fix: [src][test][docs/llm] open() does nothing once destroy() has started" and "docs: [docs/llm] the abandoned mobile native simulation plan; the owner's touch-row tests". Neither found a defect in the guard or in what its test checks. Codex Astra: "The destroy guard fixes the reported reopen bug. I found no regression in the library change." Both named the open finding MEDIUM-969 as the lifecycle problem that remains, and Codex Sol listed it as its first finding; the entry below it in this log holds what they added. Every other finding can be fixed in documentation alone, so the stop rule ended the loop after the fixes.

  - Symptom: in `ABANDONED_PLAN_MOBILE_NATIVE_SIMULATION.md`, three lines under "What cannot be done" claimed more than is true. A close button from a setting is possible, since an event handler on slot content may read the instance (Codex Sol; Codex Astra). Closing a full-screen popup on iOS is not impossible, since the app can still call `close()`; what is missing is a platform way to cancel (Codex Sol; Codex Astra). One popup per back press is not impossible in general, only not guaranteed with a watcher per select component (Codex Sol; Codex Astra). The close watcher example read the constructor from the script's own window and let a throwing constructor escape (Codex Sol). The touch example kept its flag after the open, so a later `toggle()` call got the taller rows (Codex Sol; Codex Astra). The record of the committee stated the grouping without its conditions, a fresh page for Codex Astra and used-up groups for Opus 5.5, and without the stop at a canceled close (Codex Astra); credited Codex Astra with reading the constructor from the root element's window, which it did not recommend (Codex Astra); left out the members' differing views on `dialog.showModal()` over an open popup (Codex Astra), Opus 4.8's view that `handleSlotKeydown` leaves no gap, and Codex Astra's part in the scripted-open case (Codex Sol); named no members at the unanimous tallies (Codex Sol); and dropped the owner's question whether the agent would write the code itself (Codex Sol). A finding id stood inside a sentence (Codex Astra). In this log, MEDIUM-929 still pointed to the removed `TODO.md` entry on the phone popup, and the open MEDIUM-969 had no line reference (Codex Sol). In `angularjs/API.md`, the list of calls that do not open the popup under `ll-on-open` lacked the destroyed element (Codex Sol). The new test's name began with its finding id (Codex Astra).
  - Fix: each corrected. The three claims moved from "What cannot be done" to what they are: a fact about the slots, a need for a visible way to cancel, and a guarantee that a watcher per select component cannot give. Both examples were rewritten and checked again under jsdom. The committee's record gained the conditions, the credits, the modal case and the owner's full answer.

## review (the committee on the Android back button proposal)

Process: before any code, the owner asked the committee to review the agent's proposal for a close watcher that lets the Android back button close the popup: a fresh session each of Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 4.6, Sonnet 5, Codex Sol and Codex Astra, at max effort, read-only. All seven answered. The owner then abandoned the feature with two others; `ABANDONED_PLAN_MOBILE_NATIVE_SIMULATION.md` holds the proposal, the tally and each member's position. The entries below are the findings on the code and the docs as they are, which do not depend on the proposal.

- [x] **[MEDIUM-968] - `open()` reopened a select component that `destroy()` was tearing down**
  - Symptom: `destroy()` sets `destroyed` and then closes with the reason `'destroy'`. When an `onClose` listener called `open()` there, the popup opened again, since `open()` did not test `destroyed` (Codex Astra: "`destroy()` sets `destroyed`, but `open()` never checks it."). `destroy()` went on and emptied the root element, while that open's positioner, outside-click handler and gesture listeners stayed attached and the instance counted as open. A reopen from `onClose` is a supported use, which `test/open-close-reason.test.ts` covers, so a listener that reopens at every close ran into it.
  - Fix: `open()` does nothing once `destroy()` has started, by Codex Astra's direction, "Block that reopen." `destroyed` joins the tests at the top of `open()`, which every way to open passes through: `toggle()`, the trigger's click and its keys included. The docstrings of `open()` and `destroy()` say so.
  - Verified: a test in `test/base.test.ts` with an `onClose` listener that reopens. Before the fix, `onOpen` fired a second time during `destroy()`. After it, `destroy()` leaves the popup closed, no document listener answers an outside press, and a later `open()` or `toggle()` does nothing.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-969] - A `close()` or a `destroy()` from a function that `open()` called left that open running**
  - Symptom: `open()` rendered the list and then attached the positioner, the outside-click handler and the gesture listeners, with no test in between of whether the popup was still open (Codex Astra: "An open-time rendering callback can call `close()`, yet the outer `open()` continues to listener setup."). After such a `close()`, the listeners belonged to a closed popup, and a later `close()` or `destroy()` no longer detached them, since `close()` returns early while the popup is closed; `onOpened` and `onOpen` still ran. The review of the guard against a reopen during `destroy()` widened it (MEDIUM-968). Codex Sol: a `destroy()` from a row's content function had the same effect, and so had one from an override that decides the gesture listeners. Codex Astra: a close followed by a reopen during the render was to be covered too. The agent found four more ways in while fixing: the `filterable` predicate, after which the outer call went on to show the popup of a closed select component; the gather's group functions; the arrow's content function, whose arrow of the open state stayed on the closed trigger; and the positioner's first placement, which can close the popup through `onHide` before `open()` holds the positioner.
  - Fix: the basic guard, as the owner ruled after two review rounds of a wider fix; `DESIGN.md` "Functions that build or decide" holds the ruling and how it came about. `open()` numbers its open cycle and checks, after each of its steps that runs app or subclass code, whether the select component is closed, which a destroyed one always is, or open in a newer cycle; `DESIGN.md` "In-place popup (no body portal)", "Stopped open", lists the steps. A call whose cycle is over attaches nothing more, detaches the positioner that it had just created, and skips those of `onOpened` and `onOpen` that have not run yet. The closed state of the popup moved from `close()` into one private method, `clearOpenState`. The stopped call runs it again when the select component is closed, and `destroy()` always runs it after its `close()` call, whatever that call did (MEDIUM-994). The guard promises nothing about what the popup shows then: a function that builds or decides must not change the select component. The two review rounds of the wider fix, and the seven rounds on the guard as it stands, are above (MEDIUM-975 to DOCUMENTATION-1010). Codex Sol's direction for the first fix: "recheck `this.destroyed || !this.opened` after every app-controlled phase and immediately before each global-listener attachment." Codex Astra's: "stop an obsolete opening before attaching listeners or sending open notifications, including a close followed by a reopen during rendering."
  - Verified: `test/open-superseded.test.ts`, whose cases count the listeners left on the document and on the window: a close, a destroy and a close with a reopen from a content function of the list; a close from the `filterable` predicate, from a group key function, from the arrow's content function, from each of the two gesture predicates, from `focusInitial`, from `onOpened` and from `isEmpty`; a trigger that the render moves out of view, and a listener that reopens after that; an `onOpen` listener that closes and reopens; a `destroy()` that a `close()` override does not carry out, or that meets a `close()` that throws; the active-row report of a newer open; the window scroll after a stopped call; a root that is a custom element and reacts inside the color-scheme write or a class write; a focus listener that destroys the select component at the last focus move; and, in `test/popover.test.ts`, a `beforetoggle` listener that closes inside the show, and a close inside the steps that hold the active-item report back.
  - Q: Why a counter of open cycles, not a test of `opened` alone?
    - A: Because a function can close the select component and open it again. `opened` is then true, while the outer call belongs to a cycle that is over; going on, it would attach a second set of listeners over the newer open.
  - Q: Why does a stopped call put the closed state back, when the `close()` that stopped it already did?
    - A: Because the step that ran the function goes on after the function returns: the list render commits its rows, and the arrow render commits the arrow of the open state. The closed state is one routine, so the stopped call runs it again.
  - Q: Why a guard on `open()` alone, when other calls write after app code too?
    - A: Because `open()` is the one call that attaches what outlives it: a positioner, and listeners on the document and on the window. Once those belong to a closed popup, no later `close()` removes them, since it returns early; `destroy()` did not either until it got a teardown of its own (MEDIUM-994), and an app may drop a closed select component without destroying it. An outdated row lasts until the next render.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-970] - `TODO.md` "Close reason on `onClose`" still said that `onClose()` has no argument**
  - Symptom: the entry was unchecked and said "llselect's `onClose()` has no argument", while `onClose` gets `meta.reason` (Codex Sol).
  - Fix: the entry is checked and points to `DESIGN.md` "Open and close reasons".

- [x] **[MEDIUM-795] - A mouse wheel inside the open popup scrolls the page**
  - Symptom: once the popup list reaches its top or bottom, further wheeling scrolls the page (owner report). The agent measured in headless Chromium and Firefox: a list wheeled past its end scrolls the page, in Firefox after a pause of about two seconds; a list that does not overflow, and the filter input, pass every wheel to the page. In every measured case where the page scrolled, the trigger left the view and the popup closed. Touch scrolling on llselect's popup was not measured.
  - Cause: the popup is an element of the page, so the browser passes a scroll that nothing inside the popup can take on to the page. Before the fix, the library set no `overscroll-behavior` and handled no `wheel` or `touchmove` event.
  - Fix: implemented as the owner ruled, with details that the agent decided; the positions and the rulings come first, the implementation last. The owner's position: whenever the popup is open, scrolling inside the popup, by touch on a phone or by a mouse wheel on a computer, should keep the page behind it from scrolling, whether or not the popup has a scrollbar. Inside the popup, all four chose a non-passive `wheel` guard and a non-passive `touchmove` guard, which cancel a wheel or a one-finger drag that nothing inside can scroll, and leave Ctrl+wheel and multi-touch alone. With them goes `overscroll-behavior: contain` on the list: Fable 5 and Opus 5 hold it is needed, since a `touchmove` is no longer cancelable once the list has started to scroll; Opus 4.8 calls it an optional extra layer, and Codex Sol an enhancement. All four rejected `touch-action: none` and a page scroll lock. Opus 5 alone would attach the guards to the root element, so that a wheel over the trigger while the popup is open does not scroll the page either; the other three attach them to the popup. Outside the popup, Opus 4.8, Fable 5 and Opus 5 keep today's behavior: the page scrolls, and the popup follows the trigger and closes with `'hidden'` when the trigger leaves the view. Codex Sol would close the popup at the first outside wheel, with the reason `'outside'` and without preventing the wheel, and at an outside `touchstart`; Ctrl+wheel and multi-touch zoom stay untouched, and under `outsideClickBehavior: 'block'` only the one-finger swipe and its later synthetic click are suppressed; Opus 5 noted that `'outside'` is defined as a press, so a scroll would need a close-reason decision. All four would behave the same on every platform and add no setting. On the docs, `DESIGN.md` gets the rationale (Fable 5, Opus 5) or the contract itself (Opus 4.8, Codex Sol), and the `A11Y.md` "Mouse / pointer" table gets the user-visible rows (Fable 5 and Opus 5 as the contract, Opus 4.8 as one row that points to `DESIGN.md`, Codex Sol for touch selection, pinch zoom and focus). The README gets one line (Opus 4.8 optionally, Codex Sol), one instruction for a scroller in a slot (Fable 5), or nothing (Opus 5); Fable 5 also lists `overscroll-behavior` among the CSS features above the floor in `CLAUDE.md`. The owner's tests of the native control, with wheels and swipes inside and outside the popup and on the `<select>` element itself, are in `native-select-scrolling.md`. The agent first recommended the guards on the root element and, after the owner's test of the `<select>` element itself, the guards on the popup only, both times with the list's `overscroll-behavior` and today's behavior outside the popup. A fresh Opus 5.5 session, asked at max effort with the owner's test of the `<select>` element itself in the record, attaches the guards to the root element and attaches them in `open()`, since one definition of inside already drives the outside press and the focus-out close, and since a touch-down on the trigger that closed the popup would let the following click reopen it. Outside the select component, it would close the popup at the first wheel or touch-down, with the reason `'outside'`, the same on every platform: the wheel then scrolls the page, and a touch-down follows `outsideClickBehavior`, acting under `'pass-through'` and swallowed under `'block'`; the `'hidden'` close stays as the fallback. Its reason: no native row in the record lets the page scroll under an open popup. The owner finds the guard's scope and the outside behavior hard to decide, wants to weigh them against the native record first, and is considering, for later, an optional plugin with operating-system and browser detection that, when enabled, follows the native behavior as closely as it can, perhaps the native styles too. The owner then chose the guards inside the popup only, since every native select the owner tested behaves so, and asked whether the select component should also tell a gesture inside the popup, on the trigger and elsewhere apart, so that native behaviors can be added later. On the outside behavior, the owner is weighing a design in which the native behavior of each platform and browser is a swappable function in a file of its own, starting with Firefox and Chromium on Windows. The owner also noted a near-full-screen modal on phones, an idea from earlier, and that Firefox on a Windows touchscreen makes the option rows taller, easier to tap, when a touch opens the select. The owner then asked whether each behavior should be one pure function, or each operating system plus browser one class; required the abstraction to be clean, easy to understand, easy to test, easy to use and easy to swap in; asked whether it also needs both an inheritance API and a settings API; and required consistent names. The review panel, the five members at max effort, then reviewed a design brief built on these rulings. All five recommended: three places, inside the popup, on the trigger, meaning the root element outside the popup, and elsewhere; a wheel, a one-finger touch-down and a one-finger drag, with Ctrl+wheel and multi-touch left alone; one function-valued setting read by one protected method, the customization model of `DESIGN.md`, so that an override wins and `super` reaches the setting, which answers the owner's question with both APIs and one rule; one pure function per operating system and browser, and no class; four fixed outcomes, the popup kept open or closed and the scroll let through or blocked, with no raw event; the presets in a new entry point beside `./i18n`; no detection in the first step; today's behavior outside the popup as the default; a new close reason; and, out of the first step, Chromium's touch selection, the taller rows and the phone modal. They split on six points, and the owner ruled each. The gestures inside the popup also reach the function, whose default blocks the page scroll (Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Codex Sol; Fable 5 and Opus 5.5 would fix the inside with no setting). The function runs on every gesture (Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 5.5, Codex Sol; Fable 5 would ask once per open). Listeners on the document attach only when the behavior is customized (Opus 5, which proposed a protected predicate for it; Opus 4.8; Codex Sol; Opus 5.5 would attach them on every open and measure). A touch-down on the trigger closes the popup, as the native select does, and the library swallows the click that follows (Fable 5, Opus 5.5, Codex Sol; Opus 5 would keep the popup open there). Firefox's close when a drag leaves the popup stays out of the first step (Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 5.5; Codex Sol would include it). A gesture is left alone while the visual viewport is zoomed, which Opus 5 alone raised. With the rulings the owner noted that the select component's current behavior should be expressible with these functions, and asked whether it should also be exported; and asked whether the behavior functions should see drags, with an API for the drag event, since that seems needed for the drag behaviors left out of the first step. The owner's mouse-drag tests are in `native-select-scrolling.md`. The owner then ruled the names, after the agent's proposals and example code. The type of the four outcomes is `LLSelectScrollGestureBehavior`, a behavior, not an action; its values are `'leave-popup-open-and-allow-page-scroll'`, `'leave-popup-open-and-block-page-scroll'`, `'close-popup-and-allow-page-scroll'` and `'close-popup-and-block-page-scroll'`, a string union, not an enum; the owner asked for the popup in the first value, and the agent named it in the other three too. The gesture object `LLSelectScrollGesture` has two fields: `kind`, `'wheel' | 'touch-start' | 'touch-drag' | 'touch-end'`, whose docstring, as the owner asked, says that `'wheel'` covers a mouse wheel and a touchpad; and `zone`, `'popup' | 'trigger' | 'outside'`. `'touch-end'` joins now, with a `TODO:` comment saying that it is not implemented yet, so that it is not forgotten; the agent had proposed to leave it to the drag behaviors. The owner found `kind` a generic word and took it for now. The setting is `scrollGestureToBehaviorFn`, the protected method `scrollGestureToBehavior`, and the exported default `defaultScrollGestureToBehavior`. Each behavior group gets a function of its own, not one function for every group as Qt's `eventFilter` does: the agent showed, with the repo's TypeScript 5.9.3, that one such function needs a cast when its answer type follows the group, or lets a wrong answer through when it does not, and that a group added later would reach every existing function. The code goes in a new module, `behaviors.ts` under `src/`, not in `base.ts`; the presets go in the entry point `@llselect/core/behavior-presets`, built from one file, `behavior-presets.ts` under `src/`, one object per platform, named like `behaviorPresetsOfFirefoxOnWindows` and spread into the settings. The owner renamed the entry point from `native-select-presets`, since a preset need not copy a native select. llselect's own behavior is the preset `behaviorPresetsOfLLSelectDefault` in that file, which `base.ts` imports as its default, the way it imports the English pack from `src/i18n/en.ts`; the agent had answered that the default could not live there without pulling the presets into the main bundle, and the owner pointed out that tree shaking keeps only what the main bundle imports. The agent then proposed one file per preset, after the layout of `src/i18n/`; the owner expected one file, and the agent agreed that tree shaking does not need the split. The owner chose the name `behaviorPresetsOfLLSelectDefault` over the agent's recommended `behaviorPresetsOfLLSelect`. A close by a gesture has the reason `'scroll-gesture'`, with the gesture in `meta.scrollGesture`; the owner asked whether the general information should be whether the user or the API closed the popup, and kept the ruling of `DESIGN.md` "Open and close reasons": reason only, no `source`. The protected predicate that decides whether the select component listens for scroll gestures outside itself, on the document, is `shouldListenForScrollGesturesOutside(): boolean`: the owner read the design review's `isScrollGestureObservedOutside` as "found that the gesture happened", and took the name that says what it decides. The implementation: `src/behaviors.ts` holds the types and the listeners, and `src/behavior-presets.ts` the default and the three presets, built as the `behavior-presets` files of `dist/`; `base.ts` wires the setting, the two protected methods, the close reason and the list's `overscroll-behavior`; the AngularJS directives take `ll-scroll-gesture-to-behavior-fn` and give `ll-on-close` the local `$scrollGesture`, names that the agent chose as the plain mapping of the core names. The agent also decided where the listeners sit, how the touch hold works, and the mark that lets the library recognize either copy of the default function, which `DESIGN.md` marks as the agent's. The contract is in `DESIGN.md` "Scroll gestures while the popup is open", the user-visible rows in the `A11Y.md` "Mouse / pointer" table, the README section "Wheel and touch while the popup is open", and the later steps and a pass on real devices in `TODO.md`.
  - Verified: `test/behaviors.test.ts` held 22 tests, and each of 19 code mutations failed at least one of them; after the fixes of the implementation review, it held 42 tests, and each of 37 mutations failed at least one, QUALITY-889; after round two, 52 tests and 45 mutations, QUALITY-899; after round three, 54 tests and 49 mutations, plus one mutation of the positioner that `test/positioning.test.ts` catches, QUALITY-903; after round four, two more mutations of the positioner, QUALITY-906; after round five, two more of the positioner, QUALITY-909; after round six, 55 tests and 50 mutations, plus two more of the positioner, QUALITY-912; after round seven, 55 tests and 51 mutations, plus two more of the positioner, QUALITY-915; after round eight, 55 tests and 53 mutations, plus two more of the positioner, QUALITY-918; after round nine, 56 tests and 55 mutations, QUALITY-921; after round ten, 57 tests and 57 mutations, QUALITY-923. The AngularJS test of the attribute and of `$scrollGesture` failed both wiring mutations. `npm pack --dry-run` lists the `behavior-presets` files of `dist/`. Touches in Chromium 156, sent over the DevTools protocol: a drag past the end of the list, or on a list that does not overflow, did not scroll the page; a drag outside scrolled the page with the popup left open by default, closed the popup under the Chromium preset, and closed it without a scroll under the Firefox preset; under the Chromium preset, a tap on the trigger closed the popup without reopening it, a second tap opened it, and a tap on an outside button activated the button under `'pass-through'` only. After the fixes of the implementation review, the same passes gave the same results, and new cases passed: the default preset spread from the presets bundle attached no outside listener, in all four engines; a wheel over an open shadow root in a header slot was blocked with the zone `'popup'`, in all four; and in Chromium, a tap on the arrow icon under the Firefox preset closed the popup without reopening it, after which a drag outside scrolled the page and a tap on an outside button clicked it, a tap on the clear button under the Chromium preset cleared, and a pinch that started outside after a blocking close zoomed the page. After round two, in Chromium 156, in tags mode a tap on a chip's text closed the popup without reopening it, a case that tells the old code from the new; a later tap on an outside button after a second finger, and the pinch, passed as before, regression checks that the old code passed too (Opus 5.5). Real touch devices remain, in `TODO.md`.
  - Q: Why do the popup's gestures go to listeners on the popup element itself, not only to listeners on the root element, which holds the popup?
    - A: Because Chromium 156 dispatched a wheel over the top-layer popup as not cancelable while the only non-passive listener sat on the root element: a wheel over the filter input scrolled the page 900 px, and the popup closed with `'hidden'`. Firefox 153 and both WebKit builds honored the listener on the root element, and jsdom cannot show the difference, so a test pins the listeners to the popup element.
  - Q: Why keep `overscroll-behavior: contain` on the list, when a long drag that reached the end of the list midway did not scroll the page in Chromium 156 without it?
    - A: Because the property contains what a script cannot cancel: before the listeners moved to the popup element, the same Chromium kept a non-cancelable wheel at the end of the list off the page, while such a wheel on the filter input, outside the list, scrolled the page. The drag stayed on the list because Chromium kept the whole touch scroll there; the pass on real devices checks the browsers that may not.

- [x] **[HIGH-796] - A scroll lock on `<html>` or `<body>`, or an `overflow: hidden` ancestor of a fixed-position element, keeps the popup from opening**
  - Symptom: an app built on `@llselect/core` 0.0.12 locks the page with `html:has(dialog[open]) { overflow: hidden }` while a modal `<dialog>`, centered in the viewport and holding several select components, is open. On a page shorter than the viewport, the select components in the lower half of the dialog do not open, and nothing says why; an open popup closes on the next wheel inside the dialog (the app's report). The agent reproduced in headless Chromium and Firefox: the report's case, and `body { overflow: hidden }` while `html` stays `visible`, refuse to open. With no lock, a modal dialog that is a DOM child of a 40 px tall `overflow: hidden` card refuses too, and so does a `position: fixed` drawer inside a 40 px tall `overflow: hidden` box. A trigger scrolled out of an `overflow: auto` box keeps refusing, as it must.
  - Cause: `isClippedByAncestor` (`src/positioning.ts`) treated every DOM ancestor whose computed `overflow` clips as a box that clips the trigger. The root's `overflow` applies to the viewport, not to the root's own box, and so does the body's while the root's is `visible`; Codex Sol adds that containment on `<html>` or `<body>` stops the body's propagation. A fixed-position element, a modal dialog or a popover included, escapes every ancestor that does not create a containing block for it. `open()` (`src/base.ts`) returned early on the wrong verdict, and the positioner's scroll listener closed the popup on it.
  - Fix: the owner ruled option 2 with Codex Astra's three additions ("fix: [src/positioning.ts][test] the hidden-trigger check follows the containing-block chain and ignores the root's overflow", "fix: [src/positioning.ts][test][docs/llm] the containing-block list drops container-type and measures filter once per page"; post-fix round one, MEDIUM-802 to QUALITY-805; round two, MEDIUM-809 to MEDIUM-811; round three, MEDIUM-814). The walk skips the root and a propagated body, where containment on either stops the propagation; skips an element with `display: contents`; follows the containing-block chain; stops after a top-layer element's own clip, found by `:modal`, `:popover-open` and the fullscreen element, each selector inside a `try`; and tests each axis on its own. The list of containing-block creators is the one in `DESIGN.md` "Hidden-trigger check": `container-type` is not on it, since neither `size` nor `inline-size` holds a fixed child in any engine measured, and `filter` is probed, since WebKit 18.4 does not let it hold one. The positions before the ruling: Opus 4.8, Codex Sol and Opus 5 hold that a wrong refusal is worse than a missed clip, which leaves a popup open, and Fable 5 calls a missed clip mild. Option 1, the report's fix: skip `<html>`, and skip `<body>` while the root's `overflow` is `visible` in both axes. Opus 4.8 chose it, with the modal dialog in a card and the fixed drawer recorded as known limits and option 2 left to a separate change the owner approves, since the containing-block detector is intricate and jsdom cannot test it. Option 2: option 1, plus a walk that follows the containing-block chain; Fable 5 and Codex Sol chose it. Fable 5 would take the containing-block creators from `DESIGN.md` "In-place popup", perhaps with `backdrop-filter`, and record a top-layer element under a transformed ancestor as a known limit. Codex Sol adds that the body's overflow is not propagated when `<html>` or `<body>` has containment, that the walk should test a top-layer element's own clipping and then stop (`:modal`, `:popover-open` and the fullscreen element, in guarded checks), that an ancestor clips only in the axes it clips, and that paint containment clips. Opus 5 chose a reduced form of option 2 with no list of containing-block creators: after a `position: fixed` element, skip every ancestor above it; after a `position: absolute` element, skip the static ancestors. The reduced form can only remove refusals, never add one; its cost is a missed clip, a popup that stays open, where a transformed or contained ancestor clips a fixed element. Option 3, a hit test with `elementFromPoint`: all four rejected it, since it measures covering, not clipping. Opus 4.8, Fable 5 and Opus 5 would compare against `anchor.ownerDocument`, not the global `document`. Opus 5 named `IntersectionObserver` as the candidate if this check is ever rewritten, but not now, since its first answer arrives asynchronously while `open()` refuses synchronously. The agent first recommended Opus 5's reduced form, and after the reviews of Codex Astra and Opus 5.5, option 2 with Codex Astra's three additions. The owner asked whether more checking is not better, said the owner had thought of option 2, and had Codex Astra and then a fresh Opus 5.5 session review this entry and MEDIUM-797 at xhigh effort, with a brief that carries no vote and no preference. Codex Astra ranks option 2 first, then option 1, the reduced form and option 3. It would strengthen option 2 with feature-detected top-layer checks, the containment conditions of the body's propagation and a test per axis, and holds that the reduced form encodes a known false rule, since a transformed or contained ancestor does clip a fixed element. Opus 5.5 ranks first the reduced form completed with a stop at a top-layer element whatever its position, a pass-through for `display: contents` and a test per axis; then the reduced form as listed, option 2, option 1 and option 3. It holds that option 2 as listed wrongly refuses a modal dialog inside a transformed card, since a top-layer element ignores that ancestor, and that its property list errs in both directions. Both would compare against the anchor's own document.
