- [x] **[MEDIUM-678] - the filter keystroke dropped `onFilterQueryChange` when a listener rebuilt or changed the select component while the query stood**
  - Symptom: the keystroke's guard was the stamp; a `rerender()`, a `setItems()` or a value change inside the active-row report moved it, so the keystroke returned with the query at the new text, the list filtered by it, and the app never told. Only a close resets the query.

DESIGN.md "Active item change" and the two `@internal` docstrings say which path checks what.

    - A: Because a row click names a row of the popup, and a close, a reopen, a rebuild or a value change under the active-row move replaces or empties that popup, so the row may no longer be the one the user saw; a clear or a removal names the value, which such a listener leaves meaningful. ## review (events, round two: the focus-event fixes, the active-row event, the open and close reasons)

Process: round two reviewed the round-one fixes of the select component focus events together with the second and third additions the events committee settled (`events-committee.md`): `onActiveItemChange` and `meta.reason` on `onOpen` / `onClose`. Members: Opus 5, Opus 4.8 and Codex Sol (Codex 5.5 cannot run on this account). `npm run verify` ran green before the round. One HIGH, from Codex Sol: the active-row report ran in the middle of `open()` and `close()`, so a listener that closed or reopened the select component left the outer transition to finish on a stale popup. Opus 4.8 found every round-one fix resolved and the reason threading complete at all seventeen call sites. The bridge's `on-highlight` mapping stays outside both rounds until the owner rules on it.

- [x] **[HIGH-656] - a listener of the active-row event could leave an open or a close half done**
  - Symptom: `open()` reported the initial row inside `focusInitial()`, before `onOpened`, `onOpen` and the focus move into the filter input; `close()` reported `undefined` before `onClosed` and `onClose`. A listener that closed the select component during the first, or reopened it during the second, returned into steps that then ran on the wrong popup state; a row click and a filter keystroke whose listener closed the popup went on to activate the row and to report the query change. The committee had ruled that such stale continuations are abandoned (Codex Astra).
  - Fix: the report is the last step of `open()` and of `close()`: `open()` suspends it from the render to the initial placement and reports once at its tail; `close()` reports after `onClose`. The row click activates nothing and the filter keystroke reports no query change when a listener closed the popup. Docstring, DESIGN.md "Active item change" (order and a Q&A) and `angularjs/API.md` follow. Tests: `test/active-item-change.test.ts`, two tests over the four paths.
  - Verified: `npm run verify` green; round three reads the two tails and the two guards.

The `onFocus` docstring and `angularjs/API.md` still promised the event for a click on the trigger, which contains both buttons.

Docstrings, `angularjs/API.md`, A11Y.md, DESIGN.md and the TODO passes say so. Tests: `test/focus-events.test.ts`.

## review (select component focus events: onFocus and onBlur, the AngularJS attributes and the touched flag)

Process: the events committee (`events-committee.md`) settled the design of three event additions and the owner ruled on them one at a time; the first addition, the select component focus events, landed in three commits (core, AngularJS, docs), with three earlier docs-only commits riding along for review (the three-term definitions of DOM focus, the active row and activation, and two wording fixes of the committee record). `npm run verify` ran green before the round. Round one: Opus 5, Opus 4.8 and Codex Sol (Codex 5.5 cannot run on this account). One HIGH, from Codex Sol: the focus return that `close()` now makes before hiding the popup runs trigger focus handlers before the teardown. Opus 4.8 asked the manual pass to name the `document.activeElement` timing a Tab-away close rests on; done in the TODO entry. Round two reviews the fixes below together with the second addition, the active-row event.

- [x] **[HIGH-646] - a trigger focus handler could reopen the popup inside `close()` and leave it hidden with its listeners stripped**
  - Symptom: `close()` returns focus to the trigger before its teardown; a focus handler on the trigger that calls `open()` ran with `opened` already false, set up a positioner and the outside-click listeners, and the outer `close()` then detached them, cleared the list and hid the popup while the state said open.
  - Cause: the focus return moved from the tail of `close()` to before the hide, so the hide cannot drop focus to `<body>`, with no guard for the handlers the return runs.
  - Fix: `closing` is true during the focus call and `open()` refuses while it is, like its disabled and hidden-anchor refusals; an app that opens on trigger focus no longer reopens the popup it just closed. The `open()` docstring says so. Test: `test/focus-events.test.ts`.
  - Verified: `npm run verify` green; round two reads the guard.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-647] - a mouse clear still blurred the select component**
  - Symptom: a click on the clear button focused it, the rebuilt button inherited the focus, and the theme then hid it under `data-empty`, so the browser dropped focus to `<body>` and the root `focusout` reported `onBlur`, closing an open multiple's popup, for a click inside the select component.
  - Cause: `createTriggerClearButtonEl` had no `mousedown` rule, unlike the chip's remove button it mirrors.
  - Fix: the same `preventDefault` on `mousedown`. Test: `test/focus-events.test.ts`.
  - Verified: `npm run verify` green; round two reads the button.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-648] - the ui-select bridge removed template DOM before `destroy()` detached the focus listeners**
  - Symptom: the `$destroy` handler released the row and trigger template scopes, removing their elements, before `sel.destroy()`; a focused control inside a template could fire a `focusout` on removal, in the engines that fire one, and reach `onBlur` and the touched flag during teardown, against the `angularjs/API.md` promise.
  - Fix: `sel.destroy()` first, then the scope releases.
  - Verified: the AngularJS suite green; round two reads the handler.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-649] - `onFocus` was said to precede `onOpen` without qualification**
  - Symptom: a programmatic `open()` on an unfocused select component whose filter is active fires `onOpen` first and `onFocus` after it, when the filter input takes focus; the `onFocus` docstring's firing list omitted that path, and DESIGN.md stated the order as general.
  - Fix: the docstring and `angularjs/API.md` list the path; DESIGN.md limits the order to a pointer or keyboard open and names the exception.
  - Verified: round two reads `open()` against the three texts.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-650] - "neither moves focus" was false for `setDisabled(true)` and `destroy()`**
  - Symptom: the `onBlur` docstring, `angularjs/API.md` and DESIGN.md explained the silence of the two calls by "neither moves focus"; `setDisabled(true)` on an open popup returns focus to the trigger, and `destroy()` drops focus to `<body>` when it empties the root.
  - Fix: the three texts say why neither reports a blur: the disabling moves focus inside the select component, the teardown detaches the listeners first.
  - Verified: round two reads the three texts.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-651] - the `focusedIndex` and `setFocusedIndex` docstrings misstated the `-1` case and the clamp range**
  - Symptom: `focusedIndex` said `-1` means a closed popup or no items, while an active choose-all row or action row also leaves it at `-1`; `setFocusedIndex` said the clamp runs to `items.length - 1`, while it runs over `getVisibleItems()`.
  - Fix: both docstrings.
  - Verified: round two reads them against `focusChooseAllRow`, `focusActionRow` and the clamp.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-652] - the committee record's outcome line skipped one decision, claimed sections that did not exist, and stated the owner's answers less exactly than they were given**
  - Symptom: the line ruled on seven of the eight decisions, D5 missing; said the rulings live in DESIGN.md one section per event while only the focus-events section existed; and wrote "as recommended" where the owner had answered with a letter, a question, or silence on a unanimous item.
  - Fix: the line quotes each answer as given, records D5 as not answered, and says each DESIGN.md section is written when its event ships.
  - Verified: round two reads the line against the record's decisions list.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-653] - the `$touched` entry in `angularjs/API.md` bundled three facts in one bullet**
  - Symptom: one bullet carried the flag, the class, the inside-move exception and the validation-message consequence.
  - Fix: one fact per bullet.
  - Verified: round two reads the entry.
  - Q: Why were the TSDoc bullets in `src/base.ts` and the README capability row left as they are, after the same finding named them?
    - A: Because the one-physical-line rule is for Markdown, where a renderer turns a newline into a break; TSDoc comments in `src/` wrap at the column every other docstring wraps at. The README row is a name list by design, like every other row of its table; the two-code-names limit is for prose, Q&A answers and hints.
- [x] **[QUALITY-654] - the `'block'` claim and the chip removal's focus stability had no test**
  - Symptom: the `onBlur` docstring promises no event for an outside press under `outsideClickBehavior: 'block'`, and the chip test only pinned the `preventDefault`; neither the focused host, the open popup nor the event log after a removal was asserted, though jsdom can.
  - Fix: both tests in `test/focus-events.test.ts`.
  - Verified: `npm test` green.
- [x] **[QUALITY-655] - the bridge's touched test moved focus out with `body.focus()`, which jsdom ignores, and then relied on a bare `.blur()`**
  - Symptom: the test called `body.focus()` and then `.blur()` on the filter input; round one read the second line as dead, since the first had already moved focus out.
  - Fix: a focusable outside element receives focus, as the core tests do; both old lines are gone.
  - Verified: the AngularJS suite green.
  - Q: Why not just drop the `.blur()` line, as round one asked?
    - A: Because `<body>` is not focusable in jsdom, so `body.focus()` was the no-op and the `.blur()` was the line doing the work; dropping it made the test fail. The round's reading was wrong; the suite caught it.

Process: the owner asked whether a group should get a `lang` like the items do, as DESIGN.md had foreseen with the `groupKeyToLangFn` sibling; two commits followed, the core setting and the two AngularJS attributes (`ll-item-to-lang-fn` had been missing since the item commit). Post-fix panel, round one: Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 answered; Codex 5.5 cannot run on this account ("not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account"); Codex Sol answered "model at capacity" on every try. Rounds two and three, on the documentation fixes: Opus 5, Opus 4.8 and Codex Sol; round three found every fix resolved and left only wording findings on the plan preamble and on this log. Round four, on the build fix and the records: Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 (Codex Sol at capacity) found the fixes resolved, a duplicate finding id in this log, and the pre-existing `colorScheme` omission in the same map. No HIGH finding in any round; both round-one members ruled the row inheritance right. The one MEDIUM came from `npm run verify`, not from the panel: it ran only after the rounds, because the reviewer CLIs and the verify cannot share the container's memory.

- [x] **[MEDIUM-644] - the two AngularJS lang attributes were missing from the site generator's kind map, so `build:site` and `npm run verify` failed**

  - Fix: both attributes in `NG_KINDS`.
  - Verified: `npm run verify` green after the fix; round four of the panel read the map against the headings.
  - Q: Why did three read-only panel rounds miss a build failure?

  - Q: Why MEDIUM-644, not MEDIUM-598?
    - A: Because `N` is one counter across every severity, not one per severity: 598 was already `QUALITY-598`, and the counter stood at 643 after the three DOCUMENTATION entries below.
- [x] **[QUALITY-645] - the same map omitted the `colorScheme` property heading of `defaults()`, which no guard catches**
  - Symptom: the `colorScheme` heading under `llselectConfigProvider` `defaults()` renders without a kind badge; the binding-token assert covers attribute entries only, and `kindsStrict` reports unused keys only.
  - Cause: pre-existing; the map was not updated when `colorScheme` joined `defaults()`.
  - Fix: `colorScheme: 'property'` in `NG_KINDS`.
  - Verified: `npm run verify` green after the fix.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-641] - `ll-group-key-to-lang-fn` shipped without the example pair its sibling got**
  - Symptom: `ll-item-to-lang-fn` carried a `js` and an `html` example, the group entry none, so the one non-obvious fact, that the function receives the raw `group by` value, had no example showing a `group by` clause.
  - Fix: the pair added, with `group by l.group` in the example's `ll-options`.
  - Verified: rounds two and three read the example against `NG_OPTIONS_REGEXP` and `evalFnAttr`; `npm run verify` green.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-642] - DESIGN.md "Item language" lost the reason why the count summary gets no `lang`, and never said that the trigger ignores the group's code**
  - Symptom: the group rewrite of the "where it is written" bullet dropped "pack copy in the page's language" from the count summary, leaving "mixed-language", which describes the joined value mirror; and the single select component's trigger, which sits outside the group DOM and writes only the item's own code, was not mentioned.
  - Fix: both sentences in the bullet.
  - Verified: rounds two and three read both sentences against `createGroupEl` and the single trigger's `itemToLang` write; `npm run verify` green.
  - Q: Why write the group's code on the `role="group"` container, which the rows inherit, not on the visible label?
    - A: Because the group's accessible name is the container's `aria-label`, and a name is read in the `lang` in effect on its element; the visible label is `aria-hidden`, so a code there reaches no screen reader. The rows inherit as `<option>` children of `<optgroup lang>` do, and `itemToLangFn` gives a row its own code.

## review (committee: a veto for user changes, a change reason, the item language)

Process: the owner asked whether other select libraries let an app block a pick before the value changes, and whether llselect misses any common event; the survey of 33 libraries and the owner's own use of 0.0.9 in another project (a mode select component confirmed in a modal dialog) went to a committee of six fresh read-only sessions at highest effort (Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Sonnet 4.6, Sonnet 5, Codex Sol, Codex Astra; Codex 5.5 is not supported with this ChatGPT account). Round one, two members at a time: a user-change veto ships as an `on*` event with `preventDefault()` (5:1), scope user (6:0), `reason` and `item` on `LLSelectChangeMeta` (6:0), an item-language mapping setting (6:0); 4:2 that a vetoed single-mode pick still closes the popup. Round two, three members at a time, on the popup question, on how the reason values are declared, on the setting's name and on the gate's place: close 4:2 again, but two members refuted the brief's premise that a modal opened from the handler desyncs the select component under "stay" (the `focusout` handler closes the select component when the dialog takes focus, and the HTML spec hides only auto and hint popovers when a modal opens, never a `popover="manual"` one); `as const` object for the reason values 4:2; `itemToLanguageTagFn` 6:0; entry-layer gate 6:0. The first run of round two stalled after its first batch because the runner's `wait` also waited for the memory sampler loop; the second batch ran after the fix. Record: `change-veto-committee.md`. The findings below came out of the members' verification; the documentation ones are fixed here, the two attribution findings wait for the owner's ruling, and the force-hide finding waits for a real-browser pass.

- [ ] **[QUALITY-634] - the user attribution is consumed by the first chosen-state change of a gesture, so an action row whose `onActivate` calls two setters reports `'user'` then `'api'`**
  - Symptom: `withUserChangeSource` sets `changeSource` for the whole wrapped call, but each variant's `fireChange` resets it to `'api'` before any observer runs, so only the first change of the gesture carries `'user'`.
  - Cause: the flag models "the first change of this interaction", written for the nested-setter-inside-`onChange` case, while an action row is the one wrapped path that may change the state twice.
  - Impact: any consumer that branches on `meta.source`, analytics for one, misattributes the second change; the AngularJS wrappers do not read it. `test/action-rows.test.ts` checks one change, so nothing pins either reading.
  - Fix: owner's ruling pending - scoped attribution per `withUserChangeSource` call (restore `'user'` after each `fireChange` until `fn` returns, keep the reset for nested setters inside `onChange`), or keep the consumption and state it, as the `withUserChangeSource` docstring now does.
- [ ] **[QUALITY-635] - `setItems` called first inside an action row's `onActivate` makes the reconciliation's `onChange` report `'user'`**
  - Symptom: an action row's `onActivate` that calls `setItems` first; the `onItemsChanged` reconciliation drops a chosen entry and fires `onChange` while `changeSource` is still `'user'`.
  - Cause: the same flag as QUALITY-634; the reconciliation path never forces `'api'`.
  - Impact: a consumer branching on `meta.source` gets an attribution that depends on call order; the `LLSelectChangeSource` docstring states the exception for now, pending this ruling.
  - Fix: pending with QUALITY-634; the reconciliation path can set `'api'` explicitly either way.
- [ ] **[NEEDS-VERIFICATION-636] - the force-hide premise behind `close()`'s catch block, the DESIGN.md "Force-hide resilience" bullet and the popover test rests on a spec reading the current HTML standard does not support**
  - Symptom: the comment says `dialog.showModal()` hides all popovers and that `hidePopover()` then throws `InvalidStateError`; `test/popover.test.ts` injects the throw instead of a real modal.
  - Cause: the HTML standard's "hide popovers until" steps walk the showing auto and hint popover lists only, so a `popover="manual"` element is never hidden when a modal opens, and the hide-popover algorithm returns without throwing for an already-hidden element (two committee members, round two).
  - Impact: none at runtime today (the guard is harmless), but the documented reason is wrong, and the modal-over-popup case is undocumented: when a modal takes focus outside the select component, the `focusout` handler closes it; when an overlay takes no focus, the popup stays shown; while a modal is open the rest of the document, the popup included, is inert.
  - Fix: a real-browser pass (the rootless Playwright recipe) on both behaviors, then correct the comment, the DESIGN.md bullet and the test's name, or record the browser facts if they differ from the spec.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-637] - the `onClose` docstring never said what `null` means**
  - Fix: "`null` (default) = no consumer listener.", with the hook fact in its own bullet. The `onOpen` sibling says "no consumer listener" too, since the protected hook runs either way.
  - Verified: the post-fix review read both against the `onOpened` / `onClosed` hooks; `npm run verify` green.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-638] - the `onChange` docstrings did not say that the value has already changed when it runs, that a setter may be called inside it, or that a modal may be opened from it**
  - Symptom: the owner's other project chose the revert-inside-`onChange` pattern without any public guarantee; the only statement lived in the protected `changeSource` field's docstring.
  - Fix: bullets on both variants: the trigger is already updated and the getter returns the new value; a nested setter reports `'api'`; a modal or a focus move is safe and focus that already left the select component is not reclaimed; in single mode a pick closes the popup after the handler if it is still open, while other changes leave it as it is.
  - Verified: the post-fix review read the bullets against `fireChange`, `onPopupListItemActivated`, the clear button and the `setItems` drop path, and had the closing sentence scoped to a pick and the list-render claim dropped; `npm run verify` green.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-639] - the `rerender()` docstring named only in-place item mutation, while settings functions that read external state (the page language) need it too**
  - Fix: three more bullets: the case, named by the functions that rerun; the header and footer content, which never rerun; and the filter input's pack-owned attributes, which `rerender()` cannot reach.
  - Verified: the post-fix review read it against `rerender`, the header and footer wiring and `setUiTranslationPack`; `npm run verify` green.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-640] - the `withUserChangeSource` docstring omitted the action rows and the consumption rule**
  - Fix: the list names an action row's `onActivate`, and the public `LLSelectChangeSource` and multiple-mode `onChange` lists name it too; the protected docstring states that the first chosen-state change consumes the attribution, before `onChosenChanged` runs; `LLSelectChangeSource` states the consumption rule in its own words and the reconciliation exception of QUALITY-635 (QUALITY-634 and 635 decide whether the behavior changes).
  - Verified: the post-fix review read it against `withUserChangeSource` and both `fireChange` implementations; `npm run verify` green.

## review (demo pages: section order, color-scheme showcase, nav and Dark switches)

Process: the owner asked to move the i18n sections of the demo pages to the end, with the color-scheme section before i18n and the AngularJS page's "Full source" section always last; then for a single and a multiple select component with an arrow, checkboxes and tags after the color-scheme examples; then for a Dark switch within reach while viewing them, which became one switch above each example that follows the page's color scheme; and asked why the demo pages showed Dark where the other pages show the repo link, which the demo pages never had, so their nav gained it. Each round goes to the five panel members, one at a time, read-only. Round one reached only Opus 5, on the rule and the move, before it was stopped to take in the new examples: Opus 5 fix first (two DOCUMENTATION, three QUALITY). Round two reached only Opus 5, on six commits, before it was stopped because the owner moved the Dark switch next to the examples: Opus 5 fix first (one QUALITY, three DOCUMENTATION). Round three reached all five, on seven commits, with a pause after Opus 5 for the 0.0.10 bump: Opus 5 ship (one QUALITY, two DOCUMENTATION), Opus 4.8 ship, Codex 5.5 fix first (one QUALITY), Codex Sol fix first (the same QUALITY, plus the code names on one line), Fable 5 ship (one DOCUMENTATION, the same as Opus 5's QUALITY). Round four: all five ship; Opus 5 reported one QUALITY and two DOCUMENTATION, Opus 4.8 one DOCUMENTATION. Round five: all five ship; Opus 5 reported one QUALITY. ## review (LAN URLs on make server)

Process: the owner asked `make server` to also print URLs built from this machine's current IP address, so another device on the LAN can open the site. The commit adding `scripts/print-lan-urls.mjs`, which the `serve:site` npm script runs between the site build and the python server, went to all five panel members, one at a time, read-only, since the change came from a model outside the panel. Round one: Opus 5 ship (two QUALITY), Opus 4.8 ship, Codex 5.5 fix first (one MEDIUM), Codex Sol fix first (the same MEDIUM and two QUALITY), Fable 5 ship (one QUALITY, the same as one of Opus 5's). Round two: Opus 4.8, Codex 5.5 and Fable 5 ship; Opus 5 ship (three QUALITY); Codex Sol fix first (two QUALITY, one DOCUMENTATION). Round three: Opus 4.8, Codex 5.5 and Fable 5 ship; Opus 5 fix first (two DOCUMENTATION); Codex Sol fix first (two DOCUMENTATION: one covering both of Opus 5's, one new). Round four: all five ship; Opus 5 reported three DOCUMENTATION points and Opus 4.8 one of them, all on how this log is worded, so under the stop rule they went to the owner, who ruled to fix them without another round.

- [x] **[MEDIUM-597] - when the interface lookup failed, the script threw and `make server` never started the server**
  - Cause: `networkInterfaces()` throws `ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR` where a sandbox forbids the lookup, and the npm script chains its steps with `&&`.
  - Fix: the script catches the error, prints it on a `LAN:` line and exits 0.
  - Verified: inside `codex sandbox`, the old script exited 1 with `uv_interface_addresses returned Unknown system error 1`; the new one prints that error, and the next command of an `&&` chain runs.
- [x] **[QUALITY-598] - the lines showed no interface name, so on a machine with Docker or a VPN the reader could not tell which URL another device can reach**
  - Fix: each URL line ends with its interface name, e.g. `(enp5s0)`.
  - Verified: with fake `wlan0` and `docker0` interfaces, each line names its own.
- [x] **[QUALITY-599] - on Node 18.0 to 18.3 the IPv4 filter matched nothing, so the script said the machine had no address**
  - Cause: those versions report `family` as the number 4; Node 18.4 went back to the string `'IPv4'` (the `os.networkInterfaces()` history in the Node docs).
  - Fix: the filter accepts either value.
  - Verified: with fake interfaces in the Node 18.0 shape, the script prints the IPv4 URL and skips loopback and IPv6.
  - Q: Why accept the number, not declare a Node floor that excludes those versions?
    - A: Because package.json declares no `engines` floor, and choosing one is the owner's call; the check costs one comparison.
- [x] **[QUALITY-600] - the file header restated what the code shows**
  - Fix: the restatement went. The usage line went too, as a restatement of how the script is called; its port argument came back under the port-argument entry (QUALITY-605).
  - Q: Why does the header say the script takes the port, not leave how it is called to the npm script?
    - A: Because a run without the port fails silently: it prints `:undefined` URLs, not an error. The header is where a reader looks for how to call the script.
- [x] **[QUALITY-601] - the name `info` did not say that each record describes one address assigned to an interface**
  - Fix: `addressInfo`, read from `[interfaceName, addressInfos]` pairs.
- [x] **[QUALITY-602] - the header said each printed URL "reaches the server", while the interface-name comment said another device cannot reach a Docker or VPN address, so the two comments gave opposite answers about one URL**
  - Fix: the header says the server listens on every printed address.
- [x] **[QUALITY-603] - the interface-name comment called an interface "the Wi-Fi or Ethernet line"**
  - Fix: the comment speaks of the URL a LAN device can reach.
- [x] **[QUALITY-604] - the interface-name comment said another device cannot reach a VPN address, which is false for a device on the same VPN**
  - Fix: the comment says only that Docker bridges and VPNs add addresses of their own.
- [x] **[QUALITY-605] - once the header lost its usage line, nothing said the script takes the port, so a manual run without it prints `:undefined` URLs**
  - Fix: the header says `npm run serve:site` passes the port as the only argument.
- [x] **[QUALITY-606] - with `PORT=0`, python picks a free port, while the script prints `:0` URLs**
  - Fix: none.
  - Q: Why keep the `:0` URLs, not print the port python picks?
    - A: Because the script runs before python binds, it cannot learn the picked port without starting the server itself. The README's preview recipe uses a fixed port, and python's own "Serving HTTP" line shows the port it picked.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-607] - the fix line of the interface-name entry (QUALITY-598) said "each line", while the lookup-error and loopback-only lines carry no interface name**
  - Fix: "each URL line".
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-608] - the header-restatement entry (QUALITY-600) still said the header keeps the caller's name and the bind reason "only", after the port-argument entry (QUALITY-605) added the port argument to it**
  - Fix: the fix line says the usage line went and where its port argument came back.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-609] - the header-restatement entry (QUALITY-600) kept its conclusion that only the bind reason was not obvious, after the port-argument entry (QUALITY-605) showed that the port argument was not obvious either, and no Q&A kept the lesson**
  - Fix: the title keeps the restatement only, and a Q&A says why the header names the port argument.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-610] - the `PORT=0` entry (QUALITY-606) gave its decline reason in the fix line, while the log format puts a non-obvious judgement in a Q&A**
  - Fix: the reason moved to a Q&A.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-620] - the answer of the header-restatement entry (QUALITY-600) said a run without the port "printed" `:undefined` URLs, as if the script no longer did**
  - Fix: "prints".
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-621] - the answer of the `PORT=0` entry (QUALITY-606) joined its two clauses with both "Because" and "so"**
  - Fix: "so" dropped.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-622] - the fix line of the header-restatement entry (QUALITY-600) said the usage line went, but not why it counted as a problem**
  - Fix: the line says the usage line went as a restatement of how the script is called.

An emulation in headless Chromium measured that overhead: 2.40, 21.21 and 59.24 ms per switch for 100, 1000 and 3000 select components, against 1.82, 15.70 and 51.41 ms when every select component is read first.
  - Q: Why record the measured overhead, not change the pass to read every select component first?
    - A: Because the overhead is 15 to 35 percent of the batched order's time, 0.58, 5.51 and 7.83 ms per switch at 100, 1000 and 3000 select components, not a whole-page recomputation per select component, and a scheme switch is a rare user action; a second loop and a buffer of results would add code for that gain.

- [x] **[MEDIUM-277] - the README told the app to "drop the values" of disabled items, which still submits the field name for a single select component's fixed hidden input**
  - Fix: remove or disable the hidden input instead; the `required` nuance added (the browser omits the option on submit, the required check still counts it); an item whose group is disabled counts too.
  - Q: Why a clause about group-disabled items, not a public "is this item effectively disabled" query?
    - A: Because that query is `protected` by a DESIGN decision ("not public"), and a public API change needs its own review; the clause tells the app what to reproduce. The owner can reopen that decision.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-278] - the `itemDisabledFn` docstring named methods that exist on one class only, and "the trigger still shows it" was false for the multiple count summary**
  - Fix: per-class nested lists (TypeDoc prints the base docstring under the single and multiple settings too); the count summary includes the item; `'tags'` mode shows the chip; a custom trigger content function decides; the row facts hold when the row is rendered.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-279] - the clear button, a user action that drops a disabled chosen item, was missing from the docstring and overstated in A11Y**
  - Fix: a docstring bullet; A11Y narrows "only user re-toggling is blocked" to the item itself and points to the clear-button section for the removal paths.
- [x] **[QUALITY-280] - the single-select test's post-click assertion could not fail, and the count-summary claim had no test**
  - Fix: the click assertion also checks that the popup stayed open (an activation would have closed it); the multiple retention test asserts the "1 / 3 selected" summary.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-281] - DESIGN called the submission omission "the one native behavior with no counterpart" and said llselect "has no form part"**
  - Fix: `required` named as the second behavior; "does not submit form values"; DESIGN describes what the README says.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-282] - the docstring called the clear button "the only user action" that drops a disabled chosen item, which is false for a single select component, where choosing another item replaces it, and for a disabled control**
  - Symptom: found by all four members in round three; the sentence sat in the shared part of the docstring, so TypeDoc printed it under the single settings too.
  - Fix: the single list says another choice replaces the item; the exclusivity claim was later replaced by the blocked, built-in and app paths (MEDIUM-284); the shared bullet requires `clearable` on and an enabled control; the `'tags'` facts are one per bullet; the retention fact is stated once, the native parity once.
  - Q: Why is the clear button not "the only user action" that drops a disabled chosen item?
    - A: Because a single select component replaces the item on the next choice, a disabled control blocks the button, and an action row supplied by the app may call `setChosenItems()`. The docstring now names the blocked paths (the item's own row and chip) and the built-in path with its conditions, instead of claiming exclusivity.
- [x] **[QUALITY-283] - the clear-button behavior for a disabled chosen item had no test**

- [x] **[MEDIUM-284] - the multiple list still claimed the clear button is the only user action that removes the item, while an action row may call `setChosenItems()`, `clearable` is off by default, and the button sits outside the tab order**

- [x] **[MEDIUM-302] - A11Y claimed that a focused clear button clears on Enter or Space; the trigger's keydown handler takes those keys first (open when closed, activate the focused row when open) and cancels the keydown, so no click is synthesized**
  - Fix: A11Y says the button fires only on a click or `click()` from script; a test presses Enter on the focused button and asserts the popup opened and the selection stayed.
  - Q: Why was "a focused button fires click on Enter or Space" wrong here although it holds for a plain button?
    - A: Because the keydown bubbles to the trigger's handler, which maps Enter and Space and calls `preventDefault()` before the browser would synthesize the click. A claim about what an element does is checked against the select component's own event handlers, not only against the element's DOM capability.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-303] - the drop-path entry named `toggleAll()` without its branch: its unchoose branch runs `unchooseAll()`, which preserves disabled chosen items, listed or not; and "a list that no longer contains the item" pointed at `setItems()`, which already drops such items itself**
  - Fix: `chooseAll()` and `unchooseAll()` say "a chosen item outside the current item list (`setChosenItems()` and `toggleItem()` accept such items)" and name `toggleAll()`'s choose branch only; `toggleAll()`'s own docstring states both branches (MEDIUM-310).
  - Q: Why must a claim about `toggleAll()` name the branch?
    - A: Because a method that delegates inherits the behavior of the branch it takes; "it drops" or "it preserves" is true of one branch only.
- [x] **[MEDIUM-304] - "the focus hand-off preserves that focus" did not hold for a clear: the rebuilt button is hidden by every theme while `data-empty` is true, so focus leaves it; and a click focuses a button only in some browsers**
  - Fix: A11Y limits the hand-off to re-renders that leave the button visible, says a successful clear hides it, and marks click focus as browser-dependent.
  - Q: Why was "the hand-off preserves that focus" wrong for a clear although the hand-off code does focus the rebuilt button?
    - A: Because the same render then marks the trigger empty, and every theme hides the button on that mark; a claim that an element keeps focus must account for the CSS that may hide it.

## review (theme dark color schemes, post-fix round 11)

Process: the eleventh fix batch (commit "fix: [scripts][docs] color-scheme post-fix round 10: rule 6 fixes") went to the other four panel members, one at a time, read-only. Opus 5: ship, no finding. Opus 4.8: ship, no finding. Codex 5.5: fix first, one QUALITY. Codex Sol: fix first, the same QUALITY. All four found the three outputs of the scanner in step.

- [x] **[QUALITY-276] - a backslash-newline continuation inside a quoted data URL stayed in the argument, so `%\<newline>23f00` escaped the color scan**
  - Fix: the continuation is dropped from the argument before the `data:` and color tests, as CSS drops it from the string value; the masked texts keep the source's length.

## review (theme dark color schemes, post-fix round 10)

Process: the tenth fix batch (commit "fix: [scripts][docs] color-scheme post-fix round 9: rule 6 fixes") went to the other four panel members, one at a time, read-only. Opus 5: ship, one QUALITY. Opus 4.8: ship, one QUALITY. Codex 5.5: fix first, two QUALITY. Codex Sol: fix first, three QUALITY. All four found the identifier boundary, the blank walk and the three outputs sound (one member fuzzed 100,000 inputs). The entries below merge the overlapping findings.

- [x] **[QUALITY-275] - a comment inside a url() stayed in the declaration message; a backslash-newline continuation inside a quoted url() ended the string; an escaped identifier such as `not\url(` counted as a url()**
  - Fix: the url() branch blanks the comments its blank walk skipped (a comment-like text inside the quoted argument stays); a string continues across a backslash followed by a newline (CRLF included) and ends at any unescaped newline character; a backslash before `url(` is an identifier character.
  - Q: Why is a comment inside an unquoted url(), with a `)` or `;` in it, not handled?
    - A: Because that is invalid CSS (an unquoted url token holds no comment), and the check lints the project's own theme files. The same holds for other inputs that would need a full CSS tokenizer: a theme written that way is rewritten, not accommodated.
  - Q: Why are CSS escapes other than a backslash-newline continuation (`\64 ata:` for `data:`, `\25 23` for `%23`) not decoded inside a quoted url() argument?
    - A: Because a theme author does not reach a color by writing it as a numeric escape by accident, the five theme files hold no url() at all, and decoding every escape form is the tokenizer the entry above declines. The panel's twelfth round (Opus 5) recommended recording this limit over code; the owner ratifies it.

  - Fix: the single pass records every real url() with its argument; the scan covers only `data:` URLs (an embedded image), so `url(#id)` and `url(file.svg)` are not scanned; the lookahead for a quoted argument walks the whitespace instead of slicing 16 characters.

  - Symptom: the rule changed in every round of this feature, each time verified by a throwaway script that writes a temporary theme file; `npm run check` and `npm test` exercise neither the masker nor the scanner on a crafted input.
  - Fix (owner decision pending): extract the scan into a module the test runner can import (a file next to check.mjs under scripts, exporting a function that takes a file's text and returns its problems), make `scripts/check.mjs` call it, and turn the probe's cases into a `node:test` file. Needs a place for script tests: the root runner compiles `test/**/*.ts` only.

    - A: Because a counter style named like a color misleads the reader as much as the check; the theme renames it. The check cannot tell the two apart without a CSS parser.

- [x] **[QUALITY-256] - the extended body test passed with the previous observer too, so it did not prove the removed-body fix**
  - Fix: after the new `<body>` is active, the test changes an attribute on the removed `<body>` and asserts no re-decision, then changes one on the new `<body>` and asserts the re-decision.
  - Verified: with the previous observer swapped in, the suite fails at exactly that assertion ("the removed <body> is not observed any longer", actual light); with the current one it passes.
  - Q: Why did a Verified line get written for a test that could not fail?
    - A: Because the test was written for the symptom (a new body is observed) and not for the change (the old body is not). A test that guards a fix is run against the previous code, by reasoning or by reverting, before its Verified line is written.

  - Fix: guarded like `<body>`; a detached `<html>` leaves the observer registered on nothing, and a new `<html>` is the known limit below.

Process: the third fix batch (commit "fix: [src][themes][scripts][test][docs] color-scheme post-fix round 2 fixes") went to the other four panel members, one at a time, read-only. Codex Sol: fix first, two QUALITY, three DOCUMENTATION. All four found the observer and the theme value correct; the contract text lagged. The entries below merge the overlapping findings.

- [x] **[QUALITY-250] - the observer kept a removed `<body>` referenced and kept old bodies observed**
  - Fix: on a `<body>` identity change the observer disconnects and re-registers `<html>` and the current `<body>` (none while it is missing), so a removed `<body>` is neither observed nor referenced.
  - Verified: the replaced-body test, strengthened under QUALITY-256, changes an attribute on the removed `<body>` and asserts no re-decision.
- [x] **[QUALITY-251] - the system-color keywords matched ordinary values (`transition: background .2s`, `font: menu`, `url(menu.svg)`)**
  - Fix: the literal-color scan covers only properties that accept a color (`color`, `background*`, `border*`, `outline*`, the shadows, `fill`, `stroke`, `filter`, ...) and custom properties other than `--llselect-*`, after stripping strings and `url()`.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-252] - DESIGN described the observer as attributes only, its trigger list missed a replaced or late `<body>`, and a replaced `<html>` element was not a listed limit**
  - Fix: the resolver bullet names the observation targets (the attributes of `<html>` and of the current `<body>`, the child list of `<html>`, no subtree) and the trigger; the known limits say a replaced `<html>` element is not observed again and needs `refreshColorScheme()`.
  - Q: Why not observe the document node for a replaced `<html>` as well?
    - A: Because `document.open()` and `documentElement.replaceWith()` remove every select component with the old `<html>`; a page that moves its select components into a new `<html>` is not a case worth code, and a one-line limit covers it.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-253] - the bootstrap-5 shadow comparison was wrong twice: the dark block redefines the shadow as plain black**
  - Fix: DESIGN, the divider comment in the theme and the MEDIUM-211 entry describe the dividers alone (both blocks read `--bs-body-color-rgb`); the shadow reads it in the light block only.
  - Q: Why did a wrong claim about the shadow survive two rounds?
    - A: Because the check behind the first correction read the light block only. A claim that compares one declaration with another is verified in both blocks before it is written.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-254] - wording that contradicted the code or lacked a referent**
  - Fix: `destroy()` says a further call empties the mount element again, and that collectability also needs the application to drop its references; DESIGN's bootstrap-5 note says the light focus border follows `--bs-primary-rgb` while the dark one is the literal Bootstrap itself uses in both schemes; demo 16.5 names the demo's own style.css; the `'auto'` bullet of `angularjs/API.md` is a nested list, one decision stage per item.
- [x] **[NEEDS-VERIFICATION-255] - the copy changed in this round went through the wording review**
  - Fix: Codex Astra at medium effort (the substitute for Codex Luna 6) reviewed the changed `destroy()` bullets, the demo 16.5 hint and the `ll-color-scheme` list: 4 findings, 4 applied (a repeated `destroy()` "repeats the cleanup", the demo hint names style.css and the theme's dark rule, the fallback condition of the `color-scheme` step spelled out, the reference sentence moved out of the decision list).

A probe over the five palettes measured the focused borders and the halos.
- [x] **[QUALITY-241] - a replaced <body> was never observed again, and the <head>-script repair depended on DOMContentLoaded**
  - Cause: the document is wired once; the one-shot `DOMContentLoaded` listener covered only the first appearance of `<body>`.
  - Fix: the observer also watches the child list of `<html>` (not the subtree); every callback observes the current `<body>` when it is new. That covers a `<body>` appearing after a `<head>` script and a `document.body` replaced later.

- [x] **[QUALITY-242] - the literal-color check reported each declaration one line early**
  - Cause: a declaration chunk starts with the newline left by the previous `;`.
  - Fix: the line is counted at the first non-blank character of the declaration.
- [x] **[QUALITY-243] - rule 6 matched `color-scheme` and `prefers-color-scheme` case-sensitively and knew no system colors**
  - Fix: the property name, the at-rule and the media feature match case-insensitively (the custom property `--llselect-color-scheme` stays case-sensitive, as CSS defines it); the CSS system colors join the literal-color list; keyword boundaries exclude the hyphen, so `context-menu` does not match `Menu`.
- [x] **[QUALITY-244] - the batch test asserted "none before" for one of its two select components**
  - Fix: both roots are asserted attribute-free before the microtask.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-245] - the retention statements missed two facts: the promise holds for a CLOSED instance, and `labelEl` is a second retaining element**
  - Fix: DESIGN's resolver bullet, the resolver comment and the `destroy()` docstring say: a CLOSED instance stays reachable only through its mount element and `labelEl`, like its own DOM listeners; an OPEN instance holds document listeners until `close()` or `destroy()`.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-246] - the first-check bullets of the setting docstring read as if every value queued the first check; `destroy()` promised that a further call does nothing, without the rebuild condition**
  - Fix: both scoped: a forced value is written during construction; a further `destroy()` does nothing unless a second instance was built on the element since.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-247] - the reason logged for keeping the `cancelFirstDecision` identity check was wrong**
  - Q: Why keep the identity check in `cancelFirstDecision` when `unsubscribeColorScheme` lost its own?
    - A: Because a discarded instance calls no method, so neither check serves it. The cancel check serves the unsupported path where a replaced older instance's `getColorScheme()` runs: that call does not empty the element, so a dropped newer decision would be silent. `destroy()` on that path empties the element anyway, so its check protected nothing visible.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-248] - README and demo misstated the cascade for custom colors; API.md never said what the value `auto` does; DESIGN pointed at a heading that does not exist and omitted the literal-color rule**
  - Fix: README says a rule needs the specificity of a class plus an attribute and later source order, with `.acme .llselect-root` as the example; demo 16.5 explains why its rule also names the attribute (the demo stylesheet loads before the theme) and drops the sentence that only named the wrapper; API.md states the `auto` outcome; DESIGN names "Rules for every theme file" and lists the literal-color rejection.
- [x] **[NEEDS-VERIFICATION-249] - the copy changed in this round went through the wording review**
  - Fix: Codex Astra at medium effort (the substitute for Codex Luna 6) reviewed the changed setting bullets, the changed `destroy()` bullets, the README custom-colors bullet, the demo 16.5 hint and the `ll-color-scheme` sentence: 14 findings, 14 applied (conditions as "if" sentences, the check triggers one per sentence, the retention direction stated, the README cascade rule corrected to "higher specificity, or equal specificity and a later position").

## review (theme dark color schemes, post-fix)

Process: the fix batch "fix: [src][themes][scripts][test][docs] color-scheme review round: root ownership, dark border contrast, check rule 6" went to the other four panel members for a post-fix review, one at a time, read-only, with the round below in the brief; Codex Sol also covered the whole implementation, since its first-round review never arrived. Opus 5: fix first, one MEDIUM, five QUALITY, nine DOCUMENTATION. Opus 4.8: fix first, three QUALITY, two DOCUMENTATION, one NEEDS-VERIFICATION. Codex 5.5: fix first, one MEDIUM, four QUALITY, three DOCUMENTATION. Codex Sol: fix first, three MEDIUM, five QUALITY, eight DOCUMENTATION. The entries below merge the overlapping findings.

- [x] **[QUALITY-228] - check.mjs rule 6 lost the dark block: masking brackets as letters defeated the class-name lookahead**
  - Symptom: `.llselect-root[data-llselect-color-scheme='dark']` masked to `.llselect-rootxxx...`, so the `(?![\w-])` lookahead failed and the dark block, the one place the forbidden declarations are most likely to land, went unchecked; `div.llselect-root` and `.foo.llselect-root` were still missed by the `(^|[^\w-])` prefix.
  - Fix: masking (repeated, innermost first) only locates the commas and the last combinator; the subject is tested unmasked with `/\.llselect-root(?![\w-])/`, so `.llselect-root[attr]`, `div.llselect-root`, `[attr].llselect-root` and `:is(.llselect-root)` all count, and a comma inside `:is()` or an attribute value no longer splits the list.
  - Verified: the rule rejects a copy of vanilla.css with `color-scheme: dark` added to the dark block, and passes the shipped themes.
- [x] **[QUALITY-229] - the literal-color check reported drifted line numbers and missed named colors, modern color functions and same-line declarations**
  - Cause: comments were deleted with their newlines before the lines were counted; the scan was per line and matched `#hex`, `rgb()` and `hsl()` only.
  - Fix: comments become blanks of equal length; the scan is per declaration (split on `;`), skips only properties that start with `--llselect-`, and matches hex, every color function (rgb, hsl, hwb, lab, lch, oklab, oklch, color, color-mix; case-insensitive) and the CSS named colors; `transparent` and `currentColor` stay allowed.
- [x] **[QUALITY-230] - the `<body>` observation retry needed a later subscription**
  - Symptom: one select component built from a script in `<head>` wired the document before `<body>` existed and never observed it; only a second subscription repaired that.
  - Fix: a one-shot `DOMContentLoaded` listener observed `<body>` when it was missing at wiring time; superseded by QUALITY-241, which watches the child list of `<html>` instead and covers a replaced `<body>` too.
- [x] **[QUALITY-231] - four tests were green for the wrong reason**
  - Symptom: "destroy() ends the subscription" passed because `destroy()` removes the attribute the shared pass queries; "every widget" built one select component; "one batch" cannot be observed in jsdom; the identity check in `cancelFirstDecision` had no test.
  - Fix: the destroy test puts the attribute back before the `<html>` change; the observer test builds two select components; the batch test is named for what it asserts (all decided after one microtask, none before); a new test calls `getColorScheme()` on a replaced older instance and asserts the newer instance still decides in the batch.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-232] - three statements of the no-leak promise disagreed**
  - Symptom: DESIGN and the resolver comment said the shared listeners retain nothing; the `destroy()` docstring said a discarded instance keeps deciding while its mount is in the document; the code does the latter, as the select component's own DOM listeners already do.
  - Fix: all three say the same thing: the shared listeners hold no instance; an instance stays reachable only through its mount element; once the mount leaves the document, everything is collectable, with or without `destroy()`.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-233] - two instances on one element: the supported order was undocumented, and the identity check in `unsubscribeColorScheme` guarded an unsupported path**
  - Fix: the `destroy()` docstring and DESIGN's known limits state the order (destroy first, then build) and that an older instance must not be used after a rebuild, `destroy()` included; the `unsubscribeColorScheme` identity check is removed; the claim in the constructor stays, since it covers a closed instance discarded without `destroy()`; the identity check in `cancelFirstDecision` stays for the reason under DOCUMENTATION-247.
  - Q: Why not guard every root mutation of `destroy()` with an owner token, so an older instance's `destroy()` after a rebuild is harmless?
    - A: Because the newer constructor already empties the element, and a `destroy()` that skips its teardown when it is not the owner would leave the host believing two instances are live. The supported order is cheap to follow, and a host that breaks it gets a visibly empty select component, not silent corruption.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-234] - the Tailwind table in DESIGN kept the old hover border value**
  - Fix: dark `--llselect-trigger-hover-line` is slate-400 in the table too.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-235] - the 3:1 border claim covered dividers and the tag outline, which sit near 1.4:1 in every dark palette, and omitted bootstrap-5's filter border**
  - Fix: the contrast floor in DESIGN, the TODO status and the bootstrap-5 note name the borders they cover (trigger, filter input, popup) and the focus rings; dividers and the tag outline are decorative and exempt; bootstrap-5's filter-input border is listed with its trigger border as Bootstrap's own. In the round below, the #868e96 attribution is corrected to Bootstrap 4.0's gray-600, and "like the shadow" is dropped: the dark block redefines the shadow as plain black, so the dividers alone read the variable in both blocks (the first correction, "as the shadow already does", was wrong too; DOCUMENTATION-253 holds the lesson).
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-236] - docstring sentences a developer could misread**
  - Fix: the shadow-root bullet of `refreshColorScheme()` says the page checks do not reach a shadow root and when to call; `getColorScheme()` says it decides now while the first decision is still queued (DESIGN matched); the dangling "comes last" sentence of the setting is deleted; the marks bullet lists `auto` for `data-color-scheme` and says a mark on the root itself counts; the forced-value sentence in the type docstring and in `angularjs/API.md` carries the bootstrap-5 note.
- [x] **[DOCUMENTATION-237] - README and demo wording**
  - Fix: README: "the same wrapper" became "the element your rule targets, or one of its ancestors"; "as Bootstrap documents" became "the attribute Bootstrap's own documentation uses"; the marks count on the select component's root element too; the custom-colors bullet says to load the rule after the theme stylesheet. Demo 16.5: "in both schemes" dropped, since the wrapper now resolves dark; the hint says the rule replaces the theme's light and dark values.
- [x] **[NEEDS-VERIFICATION-238] - the new copy of both fix batches had not been through the wording review the specification requires**
  - Fix: Codex Astra at medium effort (the substitute for Codex Luna 6) reviewed the changed docstrings, the README recipe, the demo hints and the `ll-color-scheme` entry after this round: 34 findings, 32 applied (the condition of each sentence spelled out, the `color-scheme` property rule as three "if" sentences, the `destroy()` docstring restructured into one lead sentence and bullets, "marks" replaced by "classes and attributes" in the README). Two declined: the `**Expression** ->` line of `angularjs/API.md` keeps the format every attribute entry there uses; the Bootstrap caveat is not repeated in the README's nested-regions bullet, since the Bootstrap bullet two lines down carries it.
  - Q: Why did the wording reviews run on Codex Astra, not on Codex Luna?
    - A: Because the session tried the model id `gpt-6-luna`, which the installed Codex CLI does not offer, and took Astra as the substitute; the CLI offers `gpt-5.6-luna`, its fast, light model. The owner then ruled that Astra is more than this review needs, and DESIGN.md names `gpt-5.6-luna`.
